entries.heading: Obituary to Norman Sharp
paras: Members were very saddened to learn of the sudden death of Norman Sharp who passed away in Sutton Coldfield on the 14 July 1977 aged 76 years old.(born in 1900).  Norman was born in Derby on 15th April 1901 and came to live in Sutton Coldfield at the age of four, when his father George Sharp moved into Sutton and joined the Club. Norman’s long association with the club commenced in 1905, a period of 72 years.  His father's performances were Norman’s main interest in the game. In 1910 Norman became 2nd Xl scorer and many of the pre-First World War score books were completed by Norman and he appears on many of the pre-First World War club team photographs. At Bishop Vesey's G.S. he passed through the various phases before he finally became captain of the school in all its sporting activities until he left in 1919.

entries.heading: Norman Sharp
paras: Norman played his first game for Sutton Coldfield C.C. in 1915 but did not become a full member until leaving school.  After a year's graduation with the "A" and 2nd teams, he became the regular 1st X1 opening right-handed batsman for the next thirty years and their captain for 8 seasons – 1941 to 1948 subsequently continued to play in the lower elevens until 1958 captaining the “A” side 1954-5, after which for the next two years he captained the Warwickshire C.C.C. Nursery Xl.

During his career Norman scored nearly 25,000 runs in club cricket, of which he scored, 19,710 runs for the Sutton of which 13,067 were for the First team, and that was before Sunday cricket arrived.  During his playing days with Sutton, he scored 19 centuries of which 15 were for the First team.  In 1923 his one appearance in first-class cricket was in 1923, when he was selected to play for Warwickshire against Worcestershire in the County Championship at Edgbaston.  He batted just once in the match, which Warwickshire won by 7 wickets, scoring 3 runs from a low batting order position, before being dismissed, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Sharp - cite_note-2 bowled by Leslie Gale.

Norman was captain of the Sutton 1st Team for eight years, and "A" team captain for four.  He rarely bowled but in one game against Aldridge C.C at Rectory Park desperate measures were required as Aldridge were 50 without loss, chasing Sutton’s moderate score of 158 for 7 wickets declared, and all the front-line bowlers had been unsuccessful and with Aldridge well behind the clock, Norman put himself on to bowl for at such times it is the captain’s privilege to toss a few up.  Norman, who was never considered a bowler of any merit did just that and the first six batsmen “holed out” in quick succession.  Having had the longest spell of bowling in his career, the openers were re-introduced into the attack, but without success, and with ten minutes remaining Norman again took the ball and secured three more victims before time was called with the Aldridge score at 95 for 9 and Norman had figures of 9 for 35.

Norman now turned his attention to the admiration of the Club, succeeded his father as fixture secretary, an office he held for eighteen years – 1930 to 1947; followed by being the treasurer for seven years - 1949 to 1955; and then to chairman - 1956 to 1962; and finally, President 1966 to 1977.

In 1956 Norman was elected an Honorable Life Member having been a member of the committee for 32 years and had undertaken many of the duties associated with the running of the club.  Throughout the period he had attended all but about half a dozen meetings and every General Meeting (except one when he was away from the district) since becoming a full member in 1919. In 1947 Norman was elected as Sutton representative on the Warwickshire County Cricket Club committee until he retired in 1972. Norman was in 1948 one of the founding members of the Midlands Club Cricket Conference and in 1954 with a membership with over 300 clubs he was elected their chairman following the retirement of Guy Heaton, of Harborne C.C.  In 1962, Norman was elected President of the M.C.C.C. an honour not only to himself but also to the club.
Norman also represented the County at hockey for several years.

entries.heading: Geoff Pritchett & Andy Blaygroves
paras: At the A.G.M. a minute silence was observed by the members in memory of our late President Norman Sharp.  A new president, Geoff Pritchett, was elected to that office.  Neil Houghton stood down as secretary and was duly thanked by the chairman with Andy Blaygroves, taking over. Michael Dixon stood down with Keith Gardom being elected as 1st Team captain.  A small number of Owls games were arranged during the latter part of the season and accordingly it was agreed that Mike Moore would captain this side if and when required.

entries.heading: Ron Smith
paras: The Annual Dinner; held on Friday 27th January in the Pavilion at Rectory Park with the Chairman Ron Smith, conducting affairs.  A toast to Sutton Coldfield C.C. was proposed by Athol Butters of M.C.C.C. & Leicester Ivanhoe C.C. which John Payne responded on behalf of the Club.  Stan Petch in a lively and humorous rendering in proposing a toast to the guests which David Dollery of Knowle & Dorridge C.C. & Warwickshire Pilgrims C.C. was equally flamboyant in his response.

entries.heading: B. K. Gardom
paras: B. K. (Keith) Gardom had decided to join the family business and retired from playing for the County side although now a 1st team player but he was the ideal man to take over from Michael Dixon as 1st Team captain and scored 1,285 runs in the season with centuries - 109 away against Harborne & 105 runs not out at home to Stratford and 102 runs not out away at Litchfield.  Michael Dixon, now after 5 years, played without the responsibility of the captaincy amassed 1,298 runs scoring 101 runs not out at home to Stratford; 109 runs not out at home to Olton; 117 runs not out at home to Bromsgrove and 120 runs at Stratford.  Graham Tidy also scored 100 runs not out at home to Aldridge.  Eight 100 in a season was a 1st team record, beating the previous record of seven in 1973.  Warwick Tidy took 6 for 40 against Mosley

entries.heading: Steve Goring
paras: Steve Goring in a 2nd Xl game against Four Oaks C.C at Rectory Park took 6 wickets for 14 runs in a 12 over spell, of which 8 were maidens.

entries.heading: James Ross & Tony Malek
paras: The1979 AGM produced very little in the way of officers relinquishing their posts other than James Ross taking over the captaincy of 2nd Team and Tony Malek looking after the Owls.

entries.heading: M Dixon & K Gardom
paras: The Club played Canada in a warm-up game before the ICC World Cup competition got on its way.  Canada was invited to bat first and scored 254 for the loss of one wicket in their 60th over before bowling Sutton out for 170.
However, Michael Dixon continued scored runs 1,109 in the season and passes 1,000 runs in a season for the 10th successive year.  Keith Gardom takes 6 for 33 against Bromsgrove

entries.heading: Haden Baker & Mark Bell
paras: Just a couple of bowling statics of note was Haden Baker’s 8 wickets for 23 runs for the seconds at Bromsgrove in 12.3 overs and 16-year-old Mark Bell taking 5 for 13 against Pickwick for the Sunday seconds. This team were runaway winners of the Midland Club Cricket Championship and received a £50 cheque from the league sponsors.

entries.heading: Peter Bell and Phil Berry
paras: The International Cricket Conference World Cup competition was held in the Midlands, who appointed the umpires for the various games within the tournament with Peter Bell and Phil Berry being appointed to officiate in 60 overs a side, USA v Sir Lanka game, at the Northampton Saints ground in Northampton.  The USA batted first and scored 168 which Sir Lanka obtained for the loss of 4 wickets scoring 170 (Peter’s photograph subsequently appeared in the publication “The Ultimate Encyclopedia of Cricket.”
Phil went on to umpire one of the semi-final games where Bermuda were all out for 181 lost to Canada who scored 186 for 6 and won by 4 wickets.

entries.heading: Ron Smith and Peter Wells
paras: At the AGM - After a period of three years as Chairman, Ron Smith stood down and Peter Wells was elected with the President paying tribute to Ron for his services to the Club.  Keith Gardom as captain for the last two years stood down to devote more time to the family business and Mike Rex Hepburn was duly elected as First team captain.

James Ross who was becoming a regular last season for the 1st team also stood down and Derrick Murphy took over the second team captaincy.  Richard Sperryn now umpiring with the first team on Sundays also stood down and Richard Glover was elected captain of both the Hawks and Grasshoppers.

The meeting also agreed that Peter Wells who ran summer cricket for the juniors decided the Peter would run a Colts Team (for under 18 boys), which had been a great success and helped in increasing the membership with the younger players getting good class of cricket, therefore it would be a committee position.

entries.heading: Mike Hepburn
paras: The Annual Dinner; held on Friday 25th January in the Pavilion at Rectory Park with the President acting as MC, a toast to Sutton Coldfield C.C. was proposed by Leslie Deakins. Secretary of Warwickshire C.C.C.  which our newly elected captain Mike Hepburn replied on behalf of the Club.  Richard Sperryn, in a humorous rendering proposing a toast to the guests which Jim Cumbes, Worcestershire C.C.C. and later Chairman of Lancashire C.C.C. replied, makes reference to being one of the last players to play both professional cricket and football.

entries.heading: Michael Dixon
paras: Michael Dixon once again completed over 1,000 runs in a season for the 11th consecutive season with a total of 1,022 runs and joined as one of three elite batsmen to score over 12,500 runs for the Club with a grand total of 12,591 and announcing his retirement at the end of the season but still managed a couple of centuries, 105 runs against Aston Unity & 110 runs against Stratford.
What a player, captain, batsman and a fine fielder positioned in the slips with a very safe pair of hands was Michael.

entries.heading: Chris Barber
paras: Chris Barber scored three centuries in the season; 101 runs at home to Loughborough Town; 104 runs away to Knowle & Dorridge; 195 runs at home to Mosley Ashfield and joined the 1,000 a season with a total of 1,169 runs.

entries.heading: Graham Williamson
paras: Another centurion was Graham Williamson with 105 runs not out at home to Aldridge and totaled 1,022 runs in the season.

entries.heading: James Ross & Mike Joseph
paras: Our fourth 1st team player to pass the 1,000 run mark was James Ross with 1,003 runs. Mike Joseph who also scores a 100 runs against Olton.

entries.heading: Rod Long
paras: The best bowling performance was a very fiery young fast bowler; Rod Long took 9 for 38 for 1st Xl against Leamington. And relative newcomer to the Club was John Robinson takes 5 for 65 against Moseley Ashfield, while in the spin department Keith Gardom took 5 for 34 against Barnt Green.

entries.heading: Mark Bell
paras: Mark Bell,playing for the Hawks continued to show good promise against Pedmore and bowling virtually unchanged taking 6 wickets for 72 runs in 16 overs.

entries.heading: John Robinson, Bob Strachan & Graham Williamson
paras: Sutton Coldfield's first team were cruelly denied their first Duncan Fearnley League victory of the season at Rectory Park on Saturday.

At Rectory Park, Sutton were poised for victory with Solihull struggling on 55 for nine when the heavens opened..The man largely responsible for putting Sutton in such a position of strength was seamer John Robinson who bowled superbly to claim seven wickets for 22. Bob Strachan also bowled well to finish with 2-28.
Sutton's out cricket was also very impressive and Graham Williamson took three fine catches. Only two Solihull batsmen managed to reach double figures. The press comment was “Solihull so lucky”

entries.heading: Chris Barber, James Ross & Keith Gardom (
paras: For the second day running, the weather spoiled Sutton's chances of getting a result at Rectory Park. this time their opponents were Milford Hall. Put in to bat, Sutton were in good form with Chris Barber hitting a sparkling 92. James Ross (50) and Keith Gardom (43) made significant contributions before Sutton made a generous declaration at 195 for three.
In-form John Robinson captured three quick wickets but the match was prematurely ended by rain.
Report taken from the Sutton Coldfield News in the summer of 1980

entries.heading: Tony Malek & Mark Hipperson
paras: With the President in the chair, there were number of changes in the elected of the committee. Tony Malek stepped down after two years as treasure and a very relative new member Mark Hipperson who was studying accountancy offered his services and he was duly elected.  The second Team had a new captain in Mike Joseph, as did the Hawkes with Richard Sperryn returning to play on Saturdays.  Mark Hipperson and another new member Michael Stokes took on the captaincy of the Grasshoppers and Owls respectively.

entries.heading: Bob Strachan
paras: The Annual Dinner was still well attended and was held in the Pavilion on Friday 30th January 1981

with our President conducting the event.  The toast to the Club was delivered by Barry Meyer Gloucestershire C.C.C. and was now on the first-class umpires list, which Graham Williamson made a warm response.

A Toast to the Guests proposed by Bob Strachan on behalf of the Club, took advantage as the doctor for several first team members, obviously having their received permissions proceeded to make some very humorous remarks about their medical ailments.  Peter Lowe, Warwickshire Pilgrims C.C. and an ex-Sutton player made a very entertaining response.

entries.heading: Chris Barber, Mark Rogers & Gavin Weston
paras: Very little regarding results or individual payers’ performances were recorded except centauries were scored by Chris Barber 108 runs; Mark Rogers with 104 runs and Gavin Weston with 101 runs.in the 1st Xl

entries.heading: Frank Lamb
paras: Vandals attacked the Score- box with a petrol bomb and it was burnt to the ground and rebuilt by Frank Lamb with members’ subscribing the funds.

entries.heading: John Robinson & James Ross
paras: There were a few changes in the officers elected for this year with John Robinson taking over as Hon Secretary from Andy Blagrove and James Ross replacing Mark Hipperson.

There were also changes in some of the team captains with Mike Joseph being responsible for both the Saturday and Sunday second teams while Andy Blagrove took over the Hawkes and R Evans the Grasshopper.

entries.heading: Mike Joseph and Don Williams
paras: The annual dinner was again held in the Club’s pavilion on Friday 29th January 82 with the President presiding over the. Evening’s event. Bob Evans from the MCCC proposing a toast to the Club and Mike Joseph responding.  Don Williams proposed a toast to the guests, which Bomber Wells, Gloucestershire & Nottinghamshire CCC’s responded.

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: The Koninklijke Nederlandse Cricket Bond or The Royal Netherlands Cricket Association or simply Holland was entertained by a strong Sutton side in a 60 over ICC warm up game.  Holland score 293 for 4 wickets before bowling the Sutton side out for 178 in the last over. Peter Bell organized the lunch arrangements with the Plough & Harrow in Slade Road, Mere Green producing a cold meal but of high quality. Peter put together a broacher, which he got W.H. Smith to sell it as it had articles from our MP, The Rector and Warwickshire CCC as well as some of the senior Club Members. It produced an income the off set the catering for the two ICC matches. The only disappointment was our President decided to go on holiday that week, but Mike Kennington stepped in to the roll of Vice President and did a great job at very short notice.

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: Sutton Coldfield hosted the ICC 60 over cup game between Canada 233 runs v USA 95 all out.  This was the 100 meeting between these two cricketing countries. Again, the catering was organized by Peter Bell with the Plough & Harrow. However, Peter had overlooked the fact that the American & Canadian have very big appetites and there was very little for our other guests.

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: Peter Bell umpired the ICC K.O. game between Kenya; who scored 210 runs for the loss of 8 wickets against Papua New Guinea who were bowled out for 173.  After the game Peter was presented with a pair of cuff links by Papua New Guinea.

entries.heading: Williamson, Hodder, Strachan, Murphy & Torry
paras: The highlight of the season was the 1st teams young spin bowler Andrew Hodder scored his maiden century of 100 runs against Fordhouse. Graham Williamson scores 105 not out against Olton at Rectory Park and Andrew Hodder at Streetly took 6 wickets for 49 runs.  Three other bowlers each took 6 wicket;, Bob Strachan for 24 runs against Stratford, Derrick Murphy for 67 runs against Ashby and Dave Torry also for 67 runs against Coventry & NW and then chipped in with 5 for 28 runs against Aston Unity.

entries.heading: George Griffith
paras: George Griffith scored a fine 115 not out on his debut for the Club against Bewdley awaywith the 2nd Xl

entries.heading: Peter Bell & George Griffith
paras: A double change occurs at the 1983 AGM with both Peter Wells and John Robinson standing down as Chairman and Treasurer respectively with Peter Bell taking on the chairmanship and George Griffith as secretary and both Peter and John were thanked by the President for Peter’s efforts over the last three years and he was duly elected a Life Member   Mike Joseph stood down as 2nd team captain, as he wished to establish a first team place, and Tony Malek was therefore appointed as 2nd team captain.  The Hawkes had a change of captaincy with Allan Southam, a relative newcomer to join the club from Water Orton C.C replacing Andy Blagroves.

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: The annual dinner was again held in the Pavilion on Friday 28th January with a toast to the Club being given by Phil Richardson for the Moseley Ashfield C.C and the chairman, Peter Bell made a witty response referring to some of the senior members’ attributes.  Andy Luckhurst proposed a toast to the guests which Guy L. Willatt. Captain of Cambridge University, Derbyshire and Scotland made an interesting response about his career in cricket
Barber,  Hodder,  Ross, Williamson, Gary Moore, Strachan, Murphy & Robinson

The 1st Xl season was somewhat disappointing having played 40 games and only won 11, and lost 9, drew 15, and abandoned 5 games, which included the M.C.C.C. Saturday League results of having played 22, won 3, lost 6, drew 9, and 4 were abandoned, although in the Sunday games better results were achieved.

Chris Barber was top of both the aggregate number of runs scored with 856 at an average of 34.2, and was followed by Andy Hodder who finished the season with 724 and an average of 31.5.  In third place was James Ross with 685 runs and an average of 22.8.  A new player to the Club was Graham Williamson with 637 runs and average of 28.9.

In the game against Leicester Ivenhoe at Rectory Park Chris Barber scored 140 runs in a 2nd wicket partnership with Mike Joseph of 176 runs with Mike contributing 54 runs.  James Ross also scored a hard worked century against Knowle & Dorridge with 113 runs & Gary Moore taking 5 wickets for 43 runs in a cliffhanger drawn game away against K&D.
Sutton batted first scoring 203 for 4 wickets and K&D in their reply finished on 200 for 9.

Andrew Hodder took 84 wickets in the season at an average of 15.2; including 4 for 3 runs against Bromsgrove; 6 for 47 @ Water Orton; & 6 for 60 runs against Stratford & 6 for 70 runs against Coventry &NW and Bob Strachan in a day game at Rectory Park against Moseley Ashfield took 5 wickets for 55 runs.

The annual Bank Holiday Tuesday encounter was a very low scoring game at Aldridge, when Sutton batting first were shot out for only 52 runs but won by 14 runs when the home club was bowled out for 38 runs with Derrick Murphy taking 5 for 8 runs and John Robinson taking 3 for 13 runs.

Therefore, looking back on the 1983 season there were many outstanding individual performances in games that deserved a better result than a draw but in league cricket it did appear that it was more important in not losing a game than winning.

entries.heading: Mark Bell
paras: Playing for the 2nd Xl, Mark Bell took 6 wickets for 22 runs.

entries.heading: Andy Hodder
paras: Andy had now blossomed out as a top-class leg spin bowler and with his quality batting made him an exceptional all-rounder in the side, he finished second in the 1st teams’ aggregate number of runs with 724 runs for the season and averaging 31.5.  In the bowling department he took 84 wickets at an average of 15.2 runs per wicket and including 4 for 3 runs against Bromsgrove; 6 for 47 at Water Orton; 6 for 60 runs against Stratford and 6 for 70 runs against Coventry & NW.  Although he was a musician studying to play the French horn, he was a fine fieldsman taking some quality catches.

entries.heading: Andy Biddle
paras: The Sutton Colts made their 1st tour East Anglia, which was organized and lead by Andy Biddle

entries.heading: Mike Kennington
paras: The only major change at the AGM was the retirement from the committee was Roger Coombs as ground secretary a post he had held since 1975 and his efforts were duly appreciated by the members and his replacement was Mike Kennington.

Dave Jackson took over as the 2nd Team captain and R. Butfield the responsibilities for the Hawks from Allan Southam and Peter Well the captaincy of the Owls as and when they had games arranged with depended on the availability but with Peter’s involvement with the younger players with the Club’s summer junior boys’ cricket

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: The annual dinner was again held in the Pavilion on Friday 27th January with Neil Abberley, Warwickshire C.C.C. proposing a toast to Club which the Chairman Peter Bell responded and propose a toast to the guests.  Tim Perkins of Blossomfield C.C. responded with several of his renderings on Black Country humour regarding “Aynuk and Ayli”. Tim was well known to Peter as Tim was a regular during the hockey season in the Blossomfield pavilion.

entries.heading: Rogers &Luckhurst
paras: Centauries by Mark Rogers, scores 110 runs against Solihull and Andy Luckhurst, who scores 103 not out against Kings Heath, and took 5 wks. for 59 runs against Harborne, and 6 for 28 runs against Coventry & NW.
The M.C.C.C. 1st XI league bowling trophy was awarded to Andy Luckhurst for an outstanding season with the ball.

entries.heading: Jackson, Robinson & King
paras: A couple of notable performances were achieved in the 2nd with both Dave Jackson and John Robinson take a hat trick during the season but the star bowler was 52-year-old Ian King taking a total of 70 wickets in the season at an average of 11.4 runs per wicket.

entries.heading: Ross, Hopper, Smethurst, Hepburn, & Williamson
paras: A number of committee changes were made at the AGM, with James Ross handing the treasurer’s position over to Mick Hooper, after holding the post for three years. Les Smethurst also stood down after taking on the fixture secretary’s position in 1972 and was replaced by Andrew Beach.  With the retirement as captain of the 1st Team Mike Hepburn, the meeting decided that Graham Williamson would be the Saturday 1st Team captain. Andy Luckhurst would captain the Club’s side in the recently formed Warwickshire Sunday League. The 3rd team (Hawks and Grasshoppers) would have the same captain and R. Evans took over both teams as captain.

entries.heading: George Griffiths & Richard Sperryn
paras: The annual dinner was again held in the Pavilion on Friday 25th January with a toast to the Club was made by A.J. Franks Esq of Aldridge CC and a response was made by George Griffiths on behalf of the Club.  A toast to the Guests was proposed by Richard Sperryn in his usually lively and humourist manner and the response by A.E.R. Cotterill Esq was delivered in a similar fashion

entries.heading: Chris Barber
paras: Chris Barber scored 94 not out in the 2nd Xl win over Leamington.

entries.heading: Andrew Beach (Obituary)
paras: Before the season began, members were shocked to learn that their Fixture secretary, Andrew Beach had passed away after a relatively short illness at the young age of 41.   Andrew known affectionately as “Chub” or “Beachey” by his many friends, both in and outside of the cricket and hockey fraternity and was held in great respect by all crickets.  As a right arm off spin bowler, he had the great ability to turn a ball sideways off a good length.  Any new batsman who had never faced Andrew before would get a ball in his first over that spun like a top, so Andrew would not bowl another big turner, but left the batsman looking for the turn.

Andrew was educated at Taunton School where he learnt his cricket and joined Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club in 1963 and in his first season, he took 94 wickets playing initially in the 2nd team where he captured 90 wickets, of which 40 were stumped by his friend Roger Coombs, getting two games in the 1st Team he took 5 for 13 runs.  Andrew was a Sutton player through and through, although he could have played for any clubs’ 1st team.  Andrew was very unfortunate that Sutton had so many ex-county spinners and several young spinners, as well as those who were well established, like Les Pellow.  Nevertheless, Andrew had many outstanding performances with the ball as in 1975 against Aston Manor in a 1st Team game he took 6 wickets for 11 runs in 10 overs of which 6 were maidens.  In another game against Aldridge Sutton were short of bowlers and Andrew bowled unchanged at one end, bowling 19 overs of which 11 were maidens and he took 6 wickets for 11 runs.  On many occasions Andrew returned 5 wickets for single figures in the run’s column.  As a left hand batsman, he always volunteered to bat at “10A” as it sounded better than last man, he was not known for batting long against a very quick bowler as the square leg umpire got in his way but against a slower ball he would attempt to put the ball out of the ground and against the Canadian National side in a 60 over a side preliminary ICC world cup game he hit two consecutive sixes on to the lower ground.

Andrew also played hockey and in the Sutton hockey club they ran a 4th team which was a social side and Andrew occupied the left-wing spot and holding the stick the wrong way round and always turned out for the away games wearing his cricket shirt and sweater and never looked like a hockey player but was the most jovial person you could play against both on and off the pitch.

Andrew was our fixture secretary at the time of his death and had three seasons as 2nd team captain 1972 to 1975 and was on the committee as the club’s social secretary in 1969 for a couple of years organizing the programme.  In one of the events, Andrew played the part of a ventriloquist dummy sitting on Graham Williamson knee, “a very funny act”.  (Note Graham passed away a few years ago after being stung by a bee which he was allergic too

Andrew was a gentleman, small in stature but big in heart, everyone was most welcome to join his company; any new member was especially welcome.  He liked a social drink and was a person who can down a pint within few seconds, however he always knew when to stop, could always tell a good story many about himself, such as his refusal to take the Club’s on field clock, which was just over two foot in diameter for its annual service in the jewellery quarter of Birmingham, because standing only 5 foot tall he would get some wag shouting at him! “Hay mate most of us carry a pocket watch”.

It can’t go unsaid that Andrew, a stalwart of the Warwickshire Pilgrims Cricket Club and was their secretary for many years and was referred to as “Super Sec”.  The Pilgrims, in those days was a touring side playing mainly in East Sussex with a cricket base at the Saffrons ground and a hotel in Eastbourne for a two-week tour.  Andrew organised the fixture for the two sides that the Pilgrims ran daily, arranged accommodation and getting players to go on tour.  A great achievement, as no game was ever cancelled by the Pilgrims.
Andrew’s life was short but he lived it to its full, and still today some 30 years later his life brings back many happy memories to those who knew him.
(Obituary by Peter Bell)

entries.heading: Graham Williamson & Les Smethurst
paras: There was only one change of officers at the AGM and that was Andy Luckhurst relinquishing the Sunday 1st Team captaincy and Graham Williamson taking it over, while retaining his position with the Saturday side.  Both Roger Coombs and Paul McCarthy were elected Life Members for their many years of service to the Club.
Les Smethurst took over the post as fixture secretary on a temporary basis following the sudden death of Andrew Beach.

entries.heading: Neil Gamble
paras: Notable games involving the 1st Team was a last ball win over Halesowen C.C., with Graham Clarke taking the last wicket of his 6 wickets for 57 runs.
He also took 5 Walsall wickets for 98 runs bowling 23 overs before Walsall declared at 215 for 5 wickets then Sutton were bowled out for 96 runs.

In a 2nd Xl game, Neil Gamble bowled Stratford out for 34 runs with Neil Gamble figures were 6 wickets for 18 runs in 12 overs, Derrick Murphy took the other 4 wickets for 16 runs in 11 overs.   Sutton winning by 7 wickets.
Sutton won the Winter 8 a side indoor league, and the Wishaw 6 a side KO competition for the second consecutive year.

entries.heading: Peter Bell & Warwick Tidy
paras: Sutton host an ICC game of 60 overs a side between Kenya who were all out for 82 runs against Zimbabwe who scored 85 runs for the loss of 3 wickets.

Peter Bell was again privileged to umpire an ICC 60 over a side game at Swindon C.C., Swindon Village, Gloucestershire between Gibraltar who were bowled out for 46 runs which Canada achieved in 3.5 overs without the loss of a wicket in getting 48 runs on a very wet wicket due to heavy morning rain causing a late start. The Sponsor of this match was Warwick Tidy as part of the Cheltenham & Gloucester building Society.

entries.heading: Andy Biddle
paras: The Sutton Colts side again organised by Andy Biddle toured Cambridgeshire & District in the August playing at Exning, March Town, Bury St. Edmunds and Camden Cricket Clubs.

entries.heading: Bob Strachan
paras: A minute’s silence was observed by the meeting in memory of the recent death of Andrew Beach and a tribute was paid by the president for Andrew’s achievement and his devotion to the club.  The AGM produced a number of changes to the committee with the chairman, Peter Bell standing down after four seasons, 1983 to 1987 and Dr. Bob Strachan was duly elected as Chairman.
Paul O’Connor took over the Fixture secretary’s role, and the thanks were recorded for Les Smethurst stepping back into the job with the sudden death of Andrew.
Graham Williams stood down as 1st Team captain and was replaced by Geoff Hopkinson with John Dodge taking over the 2nd Team from Dave Jackson, Dave also took on the role of ground secretary.

The Hawkes and Grasshoppers both had new captains Ian Wood and Steve Russell respectively and Peter Wells retaining the Owls captaincy.  The Colts tour organizer became a committee position and Richard Able taking over the responsibility from Andy Biddle.

entries.heading: Chris Barber & Neil Gamble
paras: The annual dinner was again held in the Pavilion on Friday 27th January 1987 with speeches being delivered by Chris Barber and Neil Gamble.  A toast was proposed by Bob Strachan to our guests and David Lycett from Wolverhampton C.C., made very humours response.

entries.heading: Neil Houghton
paras: W.N. (Neil) Houghton is elected as the new Treasurer of Warwickshire C.C.C. a post he goes on to hold 11 years.   The 3rd Xl wins the M.C.C.C. Championship now sponsored and known as The Chesshire Gibson League.  The Colts tour Cambridgeshire & District in August with mixed success.

entries.heading: Andrew Luckhurst, Alan Jerman & Michael Mackey
paras: The annual dinner was held at the Penns Hall Hotel on Friday 26th January with nearly a 100 members, officials and guests attended.  The highlight of the evening was the awards ceremony, with Andrew Luckhurst receiving the 1st team’s batting and bowling award. Alan Jerman took the 2nd Xl batting award and Michael Mackey receiving the bowling award.

entries.heading: Steve Russell and Ian Woods
paras: Also at the 1988 Annual Dinner, Steve Russell was voted “Clubman of the Year” and Ian Woods as captain of the 3rd Xl (The Hawks) was congratulated for the manner in the way the team had won the Chesshire Gibson League.

entries.heading: Paul O’Conner and D. Worsfold
paras: At the 1988 AGM the composition of the committee remained the same except that Paul O’Conner was leaving the district to take up an appointment in London and D. Worsfold took up the fixture secretary’s file.

entries.heading: Geoff Pritchett & Mick Hooper
paras: The club start the year off by winning the Warwickshire Winter Six-a-Side indoor league, Geoff Pritchett was “Cricketer of the Year” by the Midland Club Cricket Conference.  The 2nd Team won the Warwickshire Sunday League and the 3rd Team (the Hawks) won the M.C.C.C. league championship.  A joint 3rd Team of Hawks & Grasshoppers won the Jubilee Shield.  Mick Hooper was selected by the M.C.C Conference to play in their side against Chedworth Cricket Club, a village in the Cotswold, who were celebrating the Club’s centenary.  Mick scoring 100 runs and was not out.

entries.heading: Alan Jerman, John Dodge & Hugo Russell
paras: The 1989 AGM produced a few minor changes in the committee with some of the captains standing down.  Alan Jerman replacing John Dodge in the 2nd Team, Steve Russell took over the Hawks and retained the Grasshopper’s captaincy with Hugo Russell taking the responsibility for the Owls.

entries.heading: Peter Bell, Phil Berry & Neil Houghton
paras: The 1989 Annual general meeting took an unusual step in electing three new life members, two umpires Peter Bell and Phil Berry for their service to the club and for their honest officiating and respected decision by the club and opposition alike over many years.  A similar honour was bestowed on Neil Houghton for his many years as an outstanding player and his official administration activities within the Club and for the Warwickshire County Cricket Club.

entries.heading: Neil Houghton and Mike Hepburn
paras: A new venue was available with an attractive hire charge for our annual dinner on Friday 1st February 1989 at the Aston Wood Golf Club.  The main Speaker was Andy Lloyd Captain of Warwickshire County Cricket Club who proposed a toast to Sutton C.C.C. with replies by Neil Houghton and Mike Hepburn proposing a toast to the guest which was replied by Nattrass

entries.heading: Stephen Guy Peall
paras: Stephen (Steve) Guy Peall a young 19-year-old cricketer from Zimbabwe, born in Salisbury (now Harare) and joins the club as our first overseas professional.  He was a right arm off spin bowler and a left hand lower-order batsman who went on to play in 4 test matches for Zimbabwe and 21 One Day International between 1992 and 1996.  His four Test caps were unremarkable, with a best of 2 for 89 against Pakistan at Karachi.
Note; - While visiting the UK in 2016 Steve called into Rectory Park to renewed aquatints with many old players and friends

entries.heading: Andrew Luckhurst
paras: The Midland Club Cricket Conference elected Andy Luckhurst “Cricketer of the Year” for 1989.

The 2nd Xl win the Warwickshire Sunday League, and the 3rd Team (Hawks) win the M.C.C.C. Championship, for the third successive season, and the future starts to look very bright as the under 15’s wins the Warwickshire Under 15 League

entries.heading: Geoff Hopkinson
paras: Geoff Hopkinson, who had joined the Sutton club in 1987 after 13 years as an opening batsman with Wolverhampton who also had a spell with Coventry & N.W. in the Birmingham League, commanded a very strong side, that is on paper.  He had, according to the chairman, Bob Strachan, strengthened the 1st team that contained a former Sutton captain Mike Hepburn, a fast-scoring batsman and Graham Williamson, another ex-Sutton skipper, who also provided the impetus and support to boost the team with his hard-hitting style.

entries.heading: Andrew Luckhurst & Chris Munn
paras: The t1st , team also had one of the top midlands allrounder in Andy Luckhurst, who in his eight years with the club has developed into a fine opening batsman and is currently enjoying a great campaign with bat and ball.  Also establishing a place as Andy opening batting partner is former Streetly player Chris Munn, who is a product of Bishop Vesey Grammar School and a rugby player for the Veseyans.
Jamie Ross, Andy Biddle, Adrian Colledge & Bob McGowan,

Old Reptonian, Jamie Ross, who has played for the club for the last 20 years, continued to score runs for the first team after leading the second XI to the championship in the 1979 season.  Making a big impact, not only as a wicket-keeper, but also a prolific run-maker is Sutton Town footballer Andy Biddle, while recent additions to the first team include seam bowler Adrian Colledge (ex-Coventry & NW), and Bob McGowan, yet another local soccer player with Parkfield.
Paul Junkin, Don Collett & Steve Peall,

Two former Aston Unity players, Paul Junkin and Don Collett have also been to the fore in Sutton's bowling attack, but are a little prone to injuries at times.  Sutton has for its first time gone overseas for a young professional – a Zimbabwean off spin bowler and hard-hitting left-handed batsman Steve Peall, who at 19, played for Harare Sports in his home country and is enjoying the experience of playing here and at the same time coaching Sutton's youth players.  He has also turned out for Warwickshire Imps and the Midlands Club Cricket Conference, although his main ambition is to play for Zimbabwe and perhaps a country side next summer.

entries.heading: Danny Longhorne, Doug Hudson & Phil Sutcliffe
paras: Other new comers to join the Sutton club is all-rounder Danny Longhorne who has decided to leave Four Oaks Saints and another all-rounder in Doug Hudson who has played for Durham, together with Lancashire second team batsman Phil Sutcliffe.

entries.heading: Andrew Beach
paras: To mark the passing of Andy Beach in 1986, Mike Hepburn organized a trophy in Andrew’s memory. “The Andrew Beach Memorial Trophy” to be played in and internal competition and presented to the winning team. The idea was that whenever there was an internal competition between the two clubs – The Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club and Sutton Coldfield Hockey Club, the trophy would be presented to the winning captain before being returned to the Bar for safe keeping.  To mark the first occasion a game of cricket was organised between the current 1st Team and a team of old player drawn up by the Chairman, Bob Strachan, with the current first team running out winners.  On New Year’s Day 1st January 1990, the Cricket Club accepted a challenge from the Hockey Club for a game of hockey on the grass pitch outside the pavilion which the hockey club duly won.

entries.heading: Bob Strachan & Mike Hepburn
paras: After three years as Chairman Bob Stracham stood down and Mike Hepburn took over the Chair.  with a new secretary James Ross replacing George Griffith and Paul McCarthy replace D.T. Worsfold as fixture secretary.  Andy Luckhurst took over the 1st team captaincy from Geoff Hopkinson and Ian Nicholls accepted the Hawks captaincy.

entries.heading: Mike Hepburn
paras: The annual dinner was again held at the Aston Wood Golf Club on 1st February 1990 with Mike Hepburn in charge
Hepburn, Munn, Longhorn, Phil Sutcliffe, Luckhurst, Junkin, Collett, Hooper & Biddle

The 1st X1 results for the season were pleasing in so much that they played 53 games, of which only 1 game was abandoned, winning 23 and drew 16, with 13 games lost. However, from the editors view every member who played with the fist Xl won a match by their performance(s)..

There were some excellent games and performances, with Mike Hepburn scoring 114 not out at home to Water Orton, and 2nd wicket partnership of 154 with Chris Munn against Leamington.  Mike hit 85 not out and Chris Munn 52 runs.
Danny Longhorne scored a centaury with 133 not out away at Leamington and 86 against M&B.

Phil Sutcliffe was another centurion with 110 runs at home against Harborne and in the game against Bedworth, Sutcliffe opened the batting and carried his bat on 74 not out when Sutton were bowled out for 175 chasing 276.  He also scored 80 against Mosley Ashfield and 80 not out against Halesowen.
Another big partnership was a fourth wicket stand of 216 runs at Rectory Park against Solihull involving captain Andy Luckhurst, who hit 116 and his partner Chris Munn with 102 runs not out.

Luckhurst also figured in a 140-run partnership with Danny Longhorn at Aston Unity; Andy scoring a very quick 88 runs.  He also scored 101 runs not out against Coventry & NW and with the ball he took 7 for 84 against Stratford; 6 for 50 against Olton and 5 for 37 against Bedworth.  Andy had a major impact in every game either with the bat or ball.  Andy was well supported in the bowling attack by Paul Junkin who took 5 for 24 against Loughborough and 5 for 56 against Evesham, Don Collett taking the other 5 wickets for 47 at Evesham.
Mick Hooper in a rare 1st team game took 5 for 10 runs in 7 overs at Aldridge.  Andy Biddle as the teams’ regular wicket keeper hit a100 runs against the Old Blundellians.
Powell, Jones, Miller, Hepburn, Hart, Russell, Dunbar, Mathews, Roy, Lancaster & Cross

The 3rd X1’s, that is the combined Hawkes and Grasshoppers teams played a total of 39 Games, Won 16, Lost 10, Drew 12, Abandoned 1, of which 19 were In the Debenham, Tewson & Cheeshire League 3rd Division, winning 9 games, lost 3, drew 6, abandoned 1 finishing 4th out of the 12 teams in the league. The 4th XL, The Owls played a total of 12 Games, of which they won 3, lost 5, drew 3, and one game was abandoned
The leading run scorer was Robert Powell with a total of 844 runs at an average of 52.75, which included 102 against Shirley Park and 103 not out against Mosley Ashfield.

Against Barnt Green, A. Jones scored 203 not out and Jonathan Miller 100 not out in an unbroken 2nd wicket partnership of 287.  Centauries were scored by Steve Goring with 133 runs against Beacon, and Mike Hepburn guesting for the 3rd Team scored 113 runs against Bedworth.  C. Hart scored 100 not out against Abbotts Bromley,

Captain, Steve Russell finished the season second with the highest aggregate runs scored with a total of 513 runs at an average of 21.38.  M. Dunbar scored a total of 409 runs in 3rd place with an average of 37.12.

In the bowling department Terry Matthews took a total of 43 wickets for 847 runs at a cost of 19.7 & on 3 occasions took 5 wickets.  Justin Roy took 7 for 50 against Solihull and had 5 wickets of two occasions.  Ken Lancaster took 6 for 23 against Solihull and B.M. Cross took 7 for 16 against Streetly

entries.heading: Adrian Colledge
paras: An uneventful AGM, with only the second team captain, Alan German standing down and Adrian Colledge being duly elected in this position.

entries.heading: Alan Jerman, James Ross, Dave King, Adrian Colledge & R. Bonham
paras: The second team had an excellent season winning over 50% of the 40 games played.  Winning 21, lost 13, and drew 6,
Centauries were scored by Alan Jerman with 103 runs not out against Mosley Ashfield.

James Ross scoring 103 runs against Rugby and Dave King with 102 not out against Solihull.  Dave also took 6 wickets for 66 runs against Solihull.  Adrian Colledge took 5 for 36 runs against Evesham and 5 for 37 against Nuneaton.  R. Bonham 5 wickets for 29 against Solihull.  It should be noted that the Warwickshire Sunday League rules limited bowler to a maximum of eight overs.

entries.heading: Adan Bacher
paras: The AGM did not introduce any changes in the committee with all officers standing for election and were returned unopposed. Adam Bacher from South Africa was to be engaged as our overseas professional.

entries.heading: Geoff Pritchett & Peter Wells
paras: Geoff Pritchett announced his resignation as the Club’s President as he leaving the Midlands to live in Norfolk.

Peter Wells was elected as the Club’s new President and paid tribute to Geoff for the years of service and reminded everyone, that Geoff joining the club in 1947 direct from school and established a 1st team position as a wicketkeeper capturing 189 victims in the three season 1955 to 1956 and was a fine open batsman for many seasons.

In 1969 Geoff took on the role of second team captain for both Saturday and Sunday sides, a post he held four seasons before retiring from playing in 1966 Geoff took on the role of the club’s treasurer a post he held until 1976 and was elected our President in 1978.  A total of 47 years of playing and an officer of the club and we wish him well in his Norfolk home which was endorsed by the members.
The only other change in the committee was the election of Terry Matthews a captain of both the Hawks and Grasshoppers.

After considerable discussion and argument over subscriptions and match fees resulted in a number of alterations being finally agreed, with a £10 reduction in the annual subscription if the sub was paid before 31st May.  March fees on the lower ground would be £3.00 compared to £3.50 on the top ground.

entries.heading: Andy Luckhurst
paras: The Midland Club Cricket Championship League selected a side consisting of seven players from the Sutton club to represent them in an inter league competition against the Shropshire League.
Andy Luckhurst, captain; Paul Junkin; Richard Jerman; Mark Jerman; Andy Biddle; Chris Munn & Mike Hepburn, with James Ross travelling as 12th man.

entries.heading: Tim Buckett
paras: Tim Buckett, an Australian becomes our Overseas Professional for the 1993 season and returns for the 1994 season.

entries.heading: Andy Luckhurst & Terry Matthews
paras: 1st Xl under the captaincy of Andy Luckhurst Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club were the winners of the Willis Corroon M.C.C.C. League Championship and it is fair to say that the 1st Team of 1993 was one of the Clubs most successful sides consisting of many outstanding players in the Club’s long history, although the 1928 side against Olton & WW C.C. consisted of 7 players who had played county cricket and one for England.
The 3rd Team (the Hawks) are also winners of the Willis Corroon M.C.C.C. 3rd Xl League Championship, under the captaincy of Terry Matthew

entries.heading: Jonathan Miller
paras: In the Tuesday August Bank Holiday game at Rectory Park against Aldridge, Jonathan Miller batting 1st wicket down scored 124 not out, before Sutton declared at 194 for 6 wickets. In reply Aldridge were bowled out for 142, with Jonathan taking 5 wickets for 16 runs to give the home side a 52-run victory.

entries.heading: Andy Biddle
paras: An interesting Article by Andy on a  Visit by Knowle & Dorridge C.C in 1993
(K&D’s Chairman referred to this being their best batting side in years)

In July 1993; it appeared that the title race in the “Willis Corroon League” would be fought out between: the Royals, K & D & Barnt Green.  Sutton entertained K & D on a sunny day but the track had been affected by earlier rain.  Knowle skipper Nigel Moore (a fine all-round cricketer), affectionately nicknamed by a few of us younger members of the side as “Jimmy Hill”, owing to his remarkable resemblance to the MOTD legend, especially in the “chin” department, won the toss and inserted the home side.

The SCCC wicket was renowned for being “slow and low” and with the earlier rain, was very difficult to bat on.  We however buckled down, batting according to the conditions against a very fine attack, fronted by the hostile Darren Altree and Aussie, Kevin Bray.  Three key partnerships featured in a competitive total of 166 for 6 from 55 overs: the Jerman twins, Mark & Richard (44), Rich Jerman & yours truly (27) & then Andrew Robert Charles Biddle & John Miller (34). You won’t be surprised to hear that Michael “Rex” Hepburn made a “quick-fire” 8 before being caught, no doubt holing-out on the boundary!

I refer you to the K & D chairman’s comment in the headline, as his star-studded side, including the Warwickshire trio of: Dougie Brown, Michael Powell & Darren Altree left the posh suburb of Knowle & Dorridge C.C.  What ensued in the visitors’ innings was extraordinary to say the least. Their elite batting line-up could not deal with the unerring accuracy of seamer Adrian Sutton ably supported by the swing and pace of old man Junks.  Yes, the wicket was difficult, however 26 all out, was inexcusable, in my humble opinion.  Sutton’s figures of 10.1 overs, 6 maidens, 7 for 9 runs was incredible, the man could drop the pill on a sixpence.  He was ably supported by Paul Junkin who was rather expensive at 10 overs, 3 maidens, 3 for 16.  Let us not forget the fielding of this great side, 9 catches & an absolutely superb stumping (well you can’t disprove that, can you?).  An amazing game and we went on to win the league that year, using I believe only 15 players throughout the season. It was sad that certain ‘sour’ opposition ‘foes’ claimed our title success was due to our wicket, considering we only lost one game all season, I think that argument didn’t really stand up.

The importance of fielding was underlined in this side with some excellent out-fielders in: Mike Mackey, the Jarman’s, Christopher Munn (formerly known as Beast) & Ade Sutton, the vets: Luckhurst, Junks and Heps all had great hands, all tended to spend the majority of the season standing quite close to me within the slip cordon! PS what a fine “wickie” we had too - ask my dad.  A side note, my late father loved coming to SCCC & took up scoring, the old man’s writing was as bad as any doctors’. However, he did keep a very tidy scorebook.

I spoke to Scott Thomason (father of the legendary Thomason Twins!!) over a lager or 15 pints last season, he asked me how “my” 1st eleven side, compared with the current crop.  A cliché maybe, but it’s difficult to compare eras, as the game is so different. It was unquestionably a great side, well-balanced and a superb fielding unit. One thing the current side and the 1993 team possess(ed) in abundance, was the unquestionable camaraderie within the team, which is surely a must, for a successful side - long may that continue.

entries.heading: James Ross, Adrian Sutton & Adrian Colledge
paras: At the AGM of 1994 Adrian Sutton took over as secretary from James Ross and Adrian Colledge stood down as captain of the two’s and was replaced by James Ross.  The other main items on the agenda concerned subscriptions and match fee and was a quiet affair compared to the previous year.  No change in subscriptions, but match fees would be increased by 50 pence for all games, so that top ground games would be £4.00 and on the lower ground the fee would be £3.50.  School boys and students in full time education would not pay an annual subscription but would pay a £2.50 match fee regardless of where they played.

entries.heading: Richard & Mark Jerman and Chris Munn
paras: The 1st Xl played 52 games, including mid-week and won 23, lost 12, drew 15, with 2 games abandoned.  Centauries were scored by Richard Jerman with 143 not out against Rugby, Michael Dean scored 128 against Knowle & Dorridge; Mark Jerman scored 125 not out against Leamington, while Chris Munn was run out on 101 at Leamington.

entries.heading: Tim Buckett
paras: Tim Buckett took the bowling honours with 97 wickets in the season at an average of 15.49 runs per wicket, with an 8 for 60 against Knowle & Dorridge; and 5 for 95 against Barnt Green, bowling unchanged with 22 over and 23 over respectively.  Chris Sutton took 8 for 24 against Harborne, 5 for 44 against Mosley Ashfield and 5 for 70 against Halesowen.

entries.heading: A. Raul, Mark Jerman, Jimmy Little & George Griffith
paras: The 3rd Team had some interesting results and very good individual performances, with A. Raul being the leading run getter with 607 runs and an average of 23.35 from 28 games.
Mark Jerman scored 414 at an average of 46.0 from the 10 games he played.

entries.heading: Jimmy Little scored 306 runs with an average of 76.50 from 5 games
paras: George Griffith scored 157 runs from 3 games & was only out once – average of 157.

entries.heading: Mike Hepburn and James Ross
paras: At the 1995 AGM, Mike Hepburn and James Ross were elected Life members bring the current total of Life Members to ten.

entries.heading: Andy Luckhurst
paras: Andy Luckhurst stood down as captain of the first Team after 4 very successful seasons, not just with his captaincy but with his many outstanding performances with both the bat and the ball.

entries.heading: Adrian Sutton & Michael Mackey
paras: The first team captaincy was split again between Saturdays and Sundays with Adrian Sutton taking on the Saturday job and Michael Mackey being responsible for Sundays.

entries.heading: Paul Junkin
paras: Paul Junkin became the second team captain on both Saturdays and Sundays.

entries.heading: Terry Matthews & Simon Nicholls
paras: Terry Matthews relinquishing the Hawks captaincy in favour of Simon Nicholls but retaining the Grasshoppers captaincy.

entries.heading: Steve Russell
paras: Steve Russell would continue organizing the Club’s August tour of Cambridgeshire and surrounding areas.

entries.heading: David Trafford
paras: The chairman was pleased to announce that David Trafford, an Australian had agreed to play for Sutton as our overseas player

entries.heading: Mark Rogers
paras: The annual dinner was back in the Club’s refurbished pavilion and held on Friday 28th January with Chris Cowdrey, Kent County Cricket Club and England proposing a toast to the Club, to which Mark Rogers replied and proposing a toast to the guests with Tim Perkins, Blossomfield C.C. making a humorous and witty response including Black Country stories.
Mark Jerman, Jonathan Miller & Chris Munn,
The 1995 1st Xl highlights of 48 games played of which 17 were won, 18 lost,11 drew and 2 games were abandoned.

Mark Jerman on three consecutive Saturdays scored and attractive 144 runs away at Evesham; he was run out the following Saturday on 95 against Coventry & NW, and hit 75 runs against Cannock on the next Saturday.
Jonathan Miller scored 103 not out at home against Rugby and hit 86 runs against Harborne,
Chris Munn scored 114 not out against Moseley Ashfield, 98 runs against Moseley and 92 runs against Evesham.
Michael Dean at home to Knowle & Dorridge scored 103 runs, while at Blossomfield Michael was run out on 85 and then bowled taking 5 wickets for 30 runs.
Michael Dean in a game against Olton took 5 wickets for 35 runs with Adrian Sutton taking the other 5 wickets for 44 runs.
Adrian Sutton also had 5 wickets for 36 runs against Leamington.

entries.heading: Michael Mackey took 6 for 20 in 5.1 overs against Olton
paras: Our overseas player David Trafford also had 6 wickets for 23 runs against Solihull, which he followed up with 5 wickets for 18 in 14.4 overs at Evesham.
Sutton win the Warwickshire Sunday League John Whitehouse Trophy which is a K.O. competition.

entries.heading: Paul Greetham
paras: It was always a pleasure to welcome the Old Blundellians to Rectory Park on a Friday afternoon as part of the visitor’s week tour within Midlands Cricket and as usual they were invited to bat first, as Sutton’s 1st team was something of a scratch side.

The Sutton opening attack of Colledge and Lord were unable to get any help from a dry playing service except for a run out. However, the first change in the bowling was the introduction of Paul Greetham who got among the wickets taking 8 for 28 runs in 17 overs with the Old Boys finishing on 101 runs.
The score book did not have any information on how the Sutton side batted or was it one of those summer day that rain interfered with cricket in wat became an abandomed game.

Incidently John Holland an OB’s leg spinner, who served in the Koreen Conflict wrote about his experience in a book called the “The dying, the dead and the dammed. John also wrote a book titled “The Old Buckpassers”a light hearted story of cricket touring.

entries.heading: Jimmey Little & Steve Goring
paras: This team was also known affectionally as the Hawks on Saturdays and the Grasshoppers on Sundays had an outstanding record not on the games won but on outstanding performances by the players who played in these sides.
Centauries were scored by Jimmey Little, 129 not out away against Bromsgrove.

Steve Goring; 121 at home against Bromsgrove and 104 runs at home against Halesowen and two weeks later at home he scored another 104 runs. In the game against Harborne at Rectory Park Steve scored 50 runs with 12 fours and 2 singles.

Partnerships. In June at Bromsgrove Sutton batting first scored 241 for 2 wickets declared. The opening partnership produced 100 runs when George Griffihs was out for 31. However, Steve Goring went on to make 121 in a further partnership of 90 runs for the 2nd wicket partnership.
Steve Goring was also in an opening partnership with George Griffith of 163 against Halesowen.

entries.heading: Paul Greetham,  Ashraf, Simon Nicholls, Ken Lancaster
paras: Bowling for 3rd Xl.  In the home game against Halesowen Paul Greetham took 6 wickets for 18 runs in 14 overs winning the game by 143 runs (219 v 76)
In the Evesham match Ashraf took 7 wickets for 8 runs in 6.4 overs with Sutton winning by 192 runs (219 v 27) of which 10 were extras.

Ashraf took 5 for 41at the home game against Bromsgrove with Sutton winning by 12 runs (156 for 9 declared v 144 all out. Two weeks later at Rectory Park Ashraf took 6 for 23 runs in 10 overs (Sutton went on to win the game by 4 wickets (78 v 83 for 4)
Simon Nicholls took 5 for 43 runs away against Halesowen.to win the game by 90 runs. (210 for 6 v 120 all out)

Ken Lancaster at home took 6 for 36 against Solihull, to win the game by 97 runs (192 & 95 respectively). Away at Arlington Avenue Ken took 6 for 36 in 8 overs to win the game by 15 runs (218 for 3 declared v 160 all out).

entries.heading: Michael Dean, Andy Luckhurst & Steve Russell
paras: The AGM of 1996 produced a 1st Team captain who would be responsible for both the Saturday and Sunday sides and they elected Michael Dean, who did this job for the next three seasons.  However, the 2nd Team went the other way when Paul Junkin stood down, electing a different captain for Saturdays with Andy Luckhurst and on Sundays, Steve Russell.
Terry Matthews & Steve Nicholls,
Terry Matthews relinquished the captaincy of the Hawks and was replaced by Steve Nicholls, with Terry taking over the responsibility of the Grasshoppers. The chairman was pleased to announce that

entries.heading: Rob McLaughlin
paras: Also at the AGM the chairman announced that Rob McLaughlin, an Australian, had agreed to play for Sutton as our overseas player. The Treasurer proposed no increase in any of the subscriptions or match fees which all the members approved.

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: The annual dinner was held on Friday 26th January at the Penns Hall Hotel with 100 members and guest attending.  Our President, Peter Wells, MC for the evening.  A toast to the Sutton Cricket Club was proposed by Dr. Charles Ralston, Harborne CC, Bath RFC, & England “B” side.  Mike Hepburn replied on behalf of the Club and proposed a toast to the guests for which David Steel, Northamptonshire C.C.C., Derbyshire C.C.C. and England replied.

entries.heading: Graham Clarke
paras: Graham Clarke for the 1st Xl took 5 Walsall wickets for 98 bowling 23 overs before Walsall declared at 215 for 5 wkts, who then they bowled Sutton out for 96 runs.

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: Looking back as the Club’s historian on the High’s and Low’s following a Saturday game on the 31st August 1996 when Harborne Cricket Club visited Rectory Park and winning the toss elected to bat first and declared at tea time with a score of 239 for 3 wickets; scored in 41 overs.  Alvin Kallicharran the ex-Warwickshire & West Indian batsman was not out with 92 runs to his name.  This score was the third highest scores by any visiting team playing at Rectory Park against the 1st team.

The first occasion was when in 1935 in a two-day game against the Free Foresters who were all out for 364 runs.  The second occasion was against the Warwickshire County team in support of R. (Dick) T. Spooner benefit year that raised £188 and the County score 281 for 8 wickets, Sutton in their reply were bamboozled by the flight and spin of Eric Hollis.

Sutton in their reply to the Harborne score were all out for 33 runs in 25.5 overs, with 7 batsmen failing to score.  The top scorer was an S Potter with 11 and the next highest was extras with 9.  Sutton lost the game by 206 runs. Interesting to note that an S. Benson played for Harborne but did not get in to bat, but a D. Benson playing for Sutton failed to score a run, neither did our President of today, James Ross, who was the third batsman out with the score was 25 and 8 runs later the side were all out for 33 runs

entries.heading: Peter Bell
paras: Looking back when a new name appeared in the 2nd Xl was Andy Luckhurst opened the batting against Solihull at Marsh Lane on the 4th May 1996 scoring 128 runs not out.
On the 11th May at Mosley Ashford’s ground on Wake Green Road Andy opening the batting scored 57 not out
On the 18th May, Andy again opened the batting with 30 not out with the Sutton team winning all three games and Andy having scored a total of 215 runs without being dismissed.

However, on the 28th May, Andy was bowled by Leamington’s left arm round the wicket Clive Antrobus for naught. Nevertheless, Sutton won by one wicket with the score of 104 to Leamington and Sutton with 109 for 9 wickets being the winner by 1 wicket. Incidently Andy’s pal, Paul Junkin, made his debut game for the club and took 2 for 38 and Ashraf took 6 for 66 with both bowlers bowling unchanged for 50 overs. Each with 25 over.

In a game at home to Water Orton, the visitors scored 289 for 9 in their allotted 45 overs with Ken Lancaster taking 5 wickets for 39 runs. In reply Sutton were bowled out for 77 runs giving the visitors a 212 runs victory.

Stratford were bowled out for 34 runs with Neil Gamble bowled 12 overs, and taking 6 wickets for 18 runs and Derrick Murphy in 11 overs took 4 wickets for 16 runs.  Sutton went on to win by 7 wickets.
Simon Nicholls in the 3rd team took 4 wickets in one over, including a hat-trick against Moseley Ashfield

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: The President reminded the members that this year 1997 is the 150th anniversary of the Club’s formation and a number of special events were being arranged to mark the occasion.  The main business of the meeting was the election of the committee.  Paul McCarthy stood down as fixture secretary and was duly thanked with Erick Harding taking over the fixture responsibilities.

Andy Luckhurst and Steve Russell stood down as captains of the 2nd team on Saturday and Sunday respectively and Charles Harwood and Ken Lancaster were duly elected respectively.  Ken also took on the Sunday Hawks captaincy and N. Elvidge the Grasshoppers job.  Subscriptions had remained static for the last two seasons and the Treasurer was proposing an increase in junior members’ subscriptions as they were getting a considerable amount of cricket and his proposal that it should be increased by £5 to £15 was carried.  Luke Latimer, an Australia was engaged as our overseas player.

entries.heading: Richard Sperryn, Mike Joseph & Neil Houghton
paras: The annual dinner and our celebration of 150 years since the SCCC was formed was held on Friday 31st January at the Penns Hall Hotel with 263 members and guest attending and our President, MC for the evening.  Richard (known as Dick) Sperryn, and well known for his humoristic grace and written to suite the occasion was invited to say grace with he did with considerable humor but with just the right amount of reverence for the occasion.

The clubs’ annual playing awards for the 1996 season were made before the speeches were delivered.   Michael Joseph, who had been a playing member up to a couple of years ago before his business commitments required Mike to relocate down south, proposed a toast to the Sutton Club.

It was an outstanding rendering by Michael, mentioning many of the incidents and antidotes involving old colleagues of his playing days and he was warmly applauded by members and guest when he sat down.

A very hard act to follow, but Neil Houghton, S.C.C.C. & Warwickshire C.C.C. Chairman, rose to the occasion in his reply on behalf of the Club, with his dry humour referring to many of the guest by name as he had played alongside or against them in the past, proposing their health in his Toast.  The club had booked a well know BBC radio personality and a presenter of “Test Match Special” Henry Blofeld, who gave us all an insight into the commentary box on test match days.

It should be recorded that the menu card did not display just the meal and the speakers but in also gave a brief history of the Club; Noteworthy Jottings over 150 years; Individual Feats by players; A listing of 15 Sutton players who went on to play for Warwickshire C.C.C. and a listing of 17 major achievements by the Club during the last 20 years.

entries.heading: W.G. Grace
paras: As part of the club’s 150 years celebrations was a game against Bedminster C.C. who also were celebrating their 150th year.  One of Bedminster Cricket Clubs former members & a Vice President was Dr. W.G. Grace.  The Sutton team and supporters travel by coach to Bristol to play on the Nevile County Ground, Bristol and the game was won by Sutton.

entries.heading: James Ross
paras: After eight years as Chairman Mike Hepburn stood down in favour of James Ross, also standing down was Michael Dean and his vice-captain Jonathan Miller took on the 1st Team captaincy.
The President thanked both retirees for their years of service to the club.
Neil Houghton takes on the Treasurer position at the Warwickshire County Club.

The Birmingham League invited the Midland Club Cricket Conference League clubs, which included Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club, to join in the renamed Birmingham & District Premier Cricket League in their Division One League with promotion and relegation between the Premier and Division One Leagues.  The clubs from the Midland Combined Counties League would form Division Two.  So, Sutton Club now joined the B&DPCL, a league they had avoided having been invited several times over the previous 80 years but had always declined.

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: As part of the Club's 150th anniversary celebrations the invitation, which had been delayed 12 months due to ground development at Lord's. However, on 9th September 98 a coach pulled out of the club’s car park carrying the team and supporters lead by our President, Peter Wells and off to the Head Quarters of cricket in St John’s Wood to play the Cross Arrows, the name the MCC play under, their month of cricket.  The home side scored 273 for 7 with Miller, Dean, Roy, Lancaster and Guest all picked up wickets for Sutton.  In reply James Ross 79 and Mike Hepburn 68 gave the Sutton Club a good start, but when the final over was to be bowled the last pair Jon Miller and Ken Lancaster found themselves at the crease with 10 runs required for victory.

That target was reduced to 2 runs with one ball to be bowled, but Jon was unable to get the ball away and game was drawn at 272 for 9.  A most exciting game of cricket at the headquarters of cricket, for which the club was mentioned by the MCC captain in his after the game speech for the manner in which the Sutton Club played the game of cricket.

entries.heading: Adam Bacher
paras: Adam Bacher who was our overseas player in 1992 plays against England for South Africa in the Lord’s Test Match on 18th June 1998.  This was the 16th occasion out of the nineteen 5-day test matches that Adam played for his country.  He opened the innings and scored 22 runs but did not bat in the 2nd innings as England lost by 10 wickets.

entries.heading: Michael Dick
paras: As part of the 150 years’ celebrations, the Midland Club Cricket Conference played the Sutton club on Thursday 28th August 1998 at Rectory Park.  Unfortunately, Sutton was unable to get out a strong 1st team so they strengthened the side by inviting a number of guests to play for the Club.  However, the Club won the toss and invited the Conference to bat first but were in serious trouble losing 5 wickets for 77, mainly due to the Club’s guest player from Australia, David Frakes, who took 4 of the wickets for 40 runs in 12 overs.

However, due to some serious batting by Taylor 54 not out and Pearson 71 not out they recovered to 215 for 5 wickets before declaring, with David bowling 16 overs and finishing with 4 for 58 runs.  Sutton in their reply lost wickets at regular intervals and getting well behind the clock.  With 90 runs being required off the last 9 overs and with Sutton having lost 6 wickets, this game was now a game the Conference could not lose and a draw was the best Sutton could achieve.  That was until Frakes joined our oversea player from Zimbabwe Michael Dick, and the scoring rate picked up so that the Club required 21 runs off the last over.  Frakes hit 3 fours of the first three ball and a 4 of the filth ball, so requiring 5 off the final ball of the game, which David dispatched over long on boundary out of the ground over the groundsman’s shed.  Unbelievable, Sutton had won by 3 wickets with Michael Dick being out on 57 and David Frakes on 85 not out off 51 balls with 14 fours and 2 sixes as well as 4 for 58 off 16 overs, a remarkable performance from an outstanding cricketer.

entries.heading: Michael Dean, Michel Dick, Jonathan Miller & Paul Greetham
paras: The Club now playing in the 1st Division of the B&DPCL with the 1st team finishing 10th with 84 points in their league so just avoiding relegation, with Mosley Ashfield with 80 points & Evesham with 8 points being the unfortunate two clubs.  Michael Dean was our leading batsman (No. 24 in the top 37 with an average of over 250 runs) with 374 runs and an average of 26.71 and a highest score of 80 not out against Kings Heath.  He was closely followed by our overseas professional from Australia, Michel Dick (No. 28) with an average of 23.29 and a total of 396 runs and a highest score of 76 runs.  In the bowling we had three in the top 37 with over 15 wickets, with Jonathan Miller (No. 24) taking 37 wickets at an average of 21.37, with a best performance against Halesowen of 7 wickets for 56, bowling unchanged.  Jonathan was followed by Michael Mackey (No. 25) taking 15 wickets at an average of 21.93 with a 6 for 14 runs against Evesham.  Michael Dick (No. 34) finished the season with 35 wickets and an average of 24.17 and best performance of 5 for 79 runs against K&D.  In the Fielding with the threshold being 8 catches. Michael Dick was out on his own in top spot with 14 catches followed by Paul Greetham with 9 catches.  Out of the 22 league matches we won 6, the same number as Harborne in 4th place, but they accrued 130 points to our 81 points.  We need to look closely next season on securing additional bonus points.

entries.heading: Mike Hepburn & Justin Roy
paras: Under the same league criteria Mike Hepburn (No. 7) was the leading 2nd Xl batsman with 369 runs and with a highest score of 98 not out in the opening match at home to K&D and an average of 36.90.  In the bowling Justin Roy, (No. 17) lead the way, with 19 wickets and an average of 17.05.  The team finished in 11th position with 52 points out of the 12 teams in the league but would not be relegated as the relegation depended on where the 1st team finished

entries.heading: George Griffith, Mark Bell, Martin Ball & Ken Lancaster
paras: In the 3rd Xl George Griffith was the runner up in the 3rd Xl listing of batsmen with 350 runs and an average of 58.33 and a highest score of 70 followed by Mark Bell 3rd in the league with 260 runs and an average of 52.00, with a highest score of 77 runs.

None of the 3rd team met the bowling or fielding league’s criteria. However, the 3rd did finish a creditable 7th out of the 11 sides in their league with 108 points.  One of the best bowling performances was by 16-year-old Martin Ball at Leamington with 6 for 40 in a bowling spell of 16 overs. Ken Lancaster took 5 for 44 runs in 11 overs but lost the game against Barnt Green by 2 wickets (131 for 8 dec v 132)

entries.heading: Adam Bacher
paras: Adam Bacher who had been our overseas player in 1992 played against England for South Africa in the Lord’s Test Match on 18th June 1998.  This was the 16th occasion out of the nineteen 5-day test matches that Adam played for his country.  He opened the innings and scored 22 runs but did not bat in the 2nd innings as England lost by 10 wickets.

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: Both the Treasurer and Fixture secretaries stood down and Hugo |Russell and Ken Lancaster replaced Mick Hooper as treasurer and Eric Harding as fixture secretary respectively.  The President, Peter Wells, thanked both retirees for their diligent work.  Jon Miller relinquished the 1st Team Sunday captaincy but retained the Saturday position, with Paul Greetham taken on the Sunday captaincy.  Charles relinquished the 2nd team captaincy which split with the Chairman being elected as the Saturday captain and Naeem Arif taking on a similar position on Sundays.  Phil Mist replaced Ken Lancaster as the Hawks captain.
The Rt. Hon. Sir Norman Fowler. MP. For Sutton Coldfield was elected Hon. Vice President, and Paul Howells from Zingari C.C. in South Africa was engaged as our Club’s overseas player.

entries.heading: Paul Howells & Jonathan Miller
paras: After last season close call on the Club’s possible relegation, a number of new players were recruited to strengthen the First Team, including Paul Howells from the same South African club side Port Zingari, as last year’s overseas player Michael Dick.

Also joining the Club was wicket keeper batsman Nick Stuart and an opening batsman Jonathan Ship from Solihull, while former Kings Heath seamer John Albright has also been recruited along with placeman Richard Cross, who returns after a five break from competitive cricket.  Jonathan Miller was elected Club Captain and Michael Dean taking on the role of Senior Playing Chairman of Cricket.  Tim Robinson, whose medical studies in Sheffield are likely to prevent him from appearing regularly this season.

entries.heading: Dandy, Howells, Miller, Dean, Ship & Munn
paras: The 1st Team only just managed to survive in the B&DPL 1st Division by the smallest of margins, 1 point better off than Kings Heath, who finished 11th and were relegated along with Fordhouses, Solihull and Olton & WW.  Out of the twelve sides that competed in the last season of the Beddis Hobbs - Midland Club Cricket Championship in 1997 season, five clubs had been relegated out of Division 1.

The Club needs to look closely at speeding up their game, losing 2 points for their slow over rate, although they were unfortunate to have the highest number of abandoned games with six.  They were also very unfortunate of not being able to get over the winning line finishing 5 runs short of Kenilworth Wardens and 3 runs short against K&D and 2 runs short against Halesowen resulting in losing draws and also against Aston Unity getting only a winning draw with Unity being 9 wickets down and some 120 behind.

In the batting Richard Dandy scored 112 runs against Fordhouses in what became a Tied Game in which Sutton scored 255 for 7 wickets and Fordhouses finishing on the same score for 9 wickets down.  Richard also scored an excellent 73 against Solihull with Paul Howells in the same game scored 67 not out.  Paul had also scored 68 runs against Harborne and during the season scored over 50 runs on a number of occasions.  Captain Jonathan Miller also show his batting skills on a several occasions recording 62 runs against Harborne with his best score of 71 runs against Fordhouses.

Jonathan had an excellent game against Olton scoring an attractive 55 in Sutton score of 211 for 9 and then he took 6 for 29 runs giving Sutton a comfortable win.  Michael Dean, John Ship and Chris Munn also passed the 50-mile stone on several occasions.

The major bowling was by Paul Howells who took 50 league wickets with some excellent spells in particular in the first 3 game we played he took 5 wickets against Kings Heath, Solihull and against Olton.  However, looking at Paul’s bowling from a satirical view throughout the season shows that every 5 overs he bowled a maiden and took a wicket conceding 15 runs.  Although John Ship was the opening batsman, who had scored 73 runs in the game against Aston Unity he achieved the best bowling figures for the 1st team with 6 for 48 runs e tied game with Fordhouses.

The second team finishing 7th in their league having achieved 8 wins and 2 winning draws.  They also managed to lose 8 games and had 4 games abandoned.  However, individual performance by a number of players were outstanding, Mark Guest with a 100 not out against Old Edwardians and with his leg spin bowling at Studley with 5 for 36.  J. Kynoch scored an attractive 91 not out in a score of 180 for 2 wickets assisted by James Ross with a timely 52 runs to give the team a win over Redditch.  It is worth recording that a S. Thompson took 7 for 47 in the 2nd Team’s win over Penn and R. Day took 7 for 89 in the game against Highway.  Mick Hooper played a number game in the second team scoring 56 not out in their win over Studley.  He also played in the 3rd team and finished top of the batting averages and 3rd in the league with an average of 87.0 and an aggregate of 609 runs with a top score of 83 not out and a 74 not out.

The game against Smethwick was from Smethwick’s point of view a high scoring game when they scored 285 for 8 and Sutton in their reply managed 193 all out with Clamp scored 76 runs.  Some useful bowling performances were also achieved in the 3rd team with M. Ball taking 6 for 25 against Harborne.  However, the best performance in the 3rd Team was against West Bromwich when Sutton chased down 218 to win by 9 wickets with Brown on 91 not out and Griffin was out for 70.

entries.heading: Roger Coombs, Gavin Weston & Chris Maynard
paras: For the last 25 years the Club has always been very fortunate in having a number of quality wicket keepers (Golden Gloves) in the Club, 1960’s to the mid-1980s’ was no exception.  First with Roger Coombs, then Gavin Weston followed by Chris Maynard all three competing for the 1st team place.  As in the 1950’s Peter Lowe was kept out of the 1st team by the quality of Geoff Pritchett and Roger had to wait for Peter Lowe, who turned down an offer from Warwickshire in favour of relocating with his employer, ICI, to Bristol in 1964.
