Incidentally, one of the features of the Coseley ground was that play had to stop immediately the church bell tolled as the ground was on church land.  Richard did play a season in 1967 in the 1st team but left the game at the end of that season.

entries.heading: The Parkfield F.C. Trio
paras: In 1981 three members turned up from Parkfield Football Club and enquired about playing a little cricket.  As playing membership was low when selecting teams for the lower ground, the three, Paul A.C. O’Connor, Joe Illingworth and Robert McGowan were warmly welcomed.  What a great acquisition they were, bringing into the Hawkes, Owls and Grasshoppers cricket a new enthusiasm and team sprit from their football days, in fact they re-vitalized the Owls team.

Paul O’Connor 1982 and 83 seasons topped the Owls batting average playing 8 and 9 matches respectively with 158 runs and 157 in the second year with averages of 19.8 and 19.7.  In 1984 Paul was elected on to the General Committee and on the death of the fixture secretary, Andrew Beach in 1986, Paul took on this roll in 1987.  However, his ability was quickly recognised and he was persuaded to be involved in the NHS in the London area as their press spokesman and he left the Midlands at the end of 1987 season.

Joe Illingworth, like Paul played in the Owls in 1982 as a batsman and was only once out finished the season with an average of 57.0 and in the 1983 season Joe finished top of the Owl averages with 23.4.  During the 1984 to 87 seasons Joe was Peter Wells’ vice-captain of the Owls with a spell of captaining this side in the 1986 season.  He continued to play for the lower ground sides for a number of years before he emigrated to Malaysia in 1997, the country of his mother, although he did play a number game for the local side.

Robert McGowan affectionately referred to as Bob was the most successful player of the Parkfield players, although his quick bowling did take a few seasons to be recognised first by the two and then the 1st team in 1984 having played since 1981 in the lower sides.  Bob’s football commitments did not make him available before mid-May and finished in mid-August so his availability limited his opportunities, although he did play for the 1st team until 1989, saving his best performance for his last season against West Bromwich Nomads with 3 wickets for 20 runs.  Bob also served on the General Committee in 1984 and 85.
The Trio also brought from their football club, Richard Holland, Steve Gregg and Bob’s brother Mark who all contributed to the new enthusiasm of cricket on the lower ground.

entries.heading: John Payne
paras: John joined the Club in 1974 when working for Gulf Oil as a Lubricant Sales Engineer; he was transferred into the Midlands.  A very competent cricketer with either the bat or the ball prepared to bat in any position, and for a lesser club than Sutton he would have commanded a place in any first team either as a batsman or a bowler, as his opportunities in the 1st team were limited.  John did score centuries; in 1974 he was not out at Milford Hall with 111 runs for the 1st team and in 1979 with the 2nd team at Harborne he scored 134 runs.  His batting averages over the 6 seasons that he played for the Club was 23.8 with the 1st and with the two’s was 35.8.   John had numerous century partnerships playing with the 1st team batting at No. 5 or 6.   He also got into the Club’s record book in 1976 for getting run out on 99 in a 1st team game at home to Stratford, having taken 4 wickets for 34 runs away at Harborne also for the firsts.  At the end of the 1976 season John took a Gulf redundancy package and he and his wife set up a Guest House in Otley, Yorkshire.

entries.heading: Robert Powell
paras: Robert was another young 3rd team player in 1990 that helped the 3rd team to win 9 out of their 19 Debenham, Tewson & Cheeshire League matches, only losing 3 games.  Robert scored a total of 844 runs at an average of 52.75, which included 102 against Shirley Park and 103 not out against Mosley Ashfield.

entries.heading: Stan Petch
paras: Stan was a sales engineer based in Leeds whose head office was in Droitwich making gear tools for the agriculture market.  Stan was transferred into the Midlands and lived in Rectory Road and joined the Club after a spell with Four Oaks C.C.  He was a tall quick bowler and was a regular 2nd team player although he did make a number of appearances for the 1st team.  Stan announced his presents in the Club in 1976 when he took 7 wickets for 25 runs at Bromsgrove for the 2nd team.  In the 1979 and 80 seasons Stan took 35 and 36 wickets respectively at an average of 17.5 and 13.4 runs per wicket.  Stan was a very useful lower order batsman who believed in hitting the ball hard and in 1977 with Ray Brown 113 not out shared a partnership for the 3rd wicket of 137 runs for the Hawks against Castle Bromwich; Stan was also not out on 49.  Stan and the Family followed the Maynard’s and immigrated to live in South Africa.

entries.heading: Ross Reyburn
paras: Ross Reyburn arrived in Sutton Coldfield from North London having previously playing with Brondsbury C.C.  His new job in 1973 was as a young feature writer for the Birmingham Post & Mail and was billeted by John Robinson, alias Tiger, at Clarence Gardens in Four Oaks.  As a writer he was best known for a biography that he wrote about the early life and playing career of John Dawes, the London Welsh, British Lions (1971) and Barbarian captain.  Ross had an ‘outgoing’ personality and his frequently eccentric behaviour was a constant worry to his mother, whom, at that time, was the editor of Woman’s Journal. As far as I can recall ‘Rossey’, as he was affectionately known, did not have any real kit, regularly borrowing equipment from other players. Having found a suitable bit of wood, he did not hang about and would attack the bowling from the start.  So, he quickly made his mark in the 1st team as a top order batsman scoring just over 2,600 runs in the 1974 to 1977 seasons at an average of 23.5.  He figured in three century partnerships scoring over 50 on each occasion.  Interesting to note his only century was in 1977 scoring 102 not out against Mosley Ashfield (a club he was later to join).  Rossey considered himself to be an “all-rounder” bowling leg-breaks, although the Sutton team players did not agree.  However, in a game in 1975 against Coventry & NW, with neither of our two regular spin bowlers were able to break a sixth wicket stand of nearly 60 runs, Rossey was given the ball to bowl at Barry Flick the Warwickshire’s reserve wicket keeper and a very capable batsman.  It’s worth recording Rossey’s first three deliveries after some arm rotation exercises, he bowled his 1st delivery passing over a very surprised Barry, the second ball was best described as a “Barns Wallis” (Dam Buster Fame) bouncing three or four time before it reached Barry who enquired “Is he serious”.  The third ball was of a superb length, pitching on the leg stump and touched the outside edge of Barry’s bat to be caught behind the wicket by Gavin Weston.  Barry made some remark to which Rossey replied “Yes! I am very serious”.

Ross moved from Sutton to live in Moseley and joined the Ashfield Club.  So, it was always a delight to meet up with Rossey on our Bank Holiday game against Ashfield renewing old acquaintances.  One such a day, when rain prevented any play before lunch, Chris Barber and Ross disagreed on who could run across the Ashfield ground from the entrance gate to the pavilion the quickest.  Rossey’s challenge was accept when his bet of five pound was proposed.  However, Ross introduced two rules, insisted that it should be a blindfold event and with three rotations of each contestant.  Barber going first was off running with cheers and applause from the pavilion, in what was considered a good time.  However, after Ross was blinded folded and rotated, he was off running, but those watching moved down towards the golf course adjacent to the ground cheering and applauding as Ross followed the sound ending in the club’s nets some 50 meters from the pavilion and well behind the time set by Chris.  Ross was finally disqualified for cheating as he was seen lifting the eye covering to see why he was in the netting.

entries.heading: A. Rauf
paras: Abdual Raul was top of the 3rd teams batting aggregate in 1994 with 607 runs and an average of 23.35 from 28 games.  Sadly, he passed away with a brain cancer.

entries.heading: Antony Robinson
paras: Tony Robinson, a Rhodesian now Zimbabwe, was in the UK on a three-year contract with the NHS at Good Hope as a Gynecologist, and joined the Club in 1969 as a patient attractive batsman with a wide range of strokes, but due to his availability his opportunities were limited.  However, he did score two centuries, 106 runs, not out at home to Olton and away at Harborne he scored 101 runs, not out in 71 minutes.   By the time he returned home at the end of the 1971 season Tony had figured in 5 century partnerships where he was not out and the game was won.   Incidentally Tony was an excellent wicket keeper, but had no real opportunities at Sutton

entries.heading: John Robinson – Life Member
paras: John left Huyton, Nr. Liverpool, Prime Minister Harold Wilson’s constituency, when he was appointed manager of the department of Chemical Pathology at Good Hope Hospital in February 1970.  John joined the Club as a consequence of a ‘beer match’ between the Club and the Hospital Staff, when his previous cricketing experience was noted.  After the match he exchanged several pints of beer with Andrew Beach and Roger Coombs and joined the Club in 1971. John acquired the nickname ‘Tiger’ and nobody is quite sure why. One possibility is that a lady spotted a pair of striped underpants amongst his kit, but a more likely explanation is a comment on his ‘mock’ aggression when running in to bowl!

He played in the 1st team and laboured regularly up the hill when opening the bowling during home games.   He had occasional 5-wicket hauls with his medium-quick swing and seam bowling and was part of the championship-winning team in 1977, during which season his best analysis was 7 for 22 against Solihull.  In 1984 he played against Ashby Hastings and captured 6 wickets for 24 runs including the Hat-Trick.

As a sociable player with better- than-average ability and a good sense of humour, and was invited to join the Warwickshire Pilgrims and also Warwickshire Imps. Tiger toured with Warwickshire Pilgrims for many years and was entrusted to be their Treasurer for most of that time, he also toured a couple of years with the Mayflies.

With the cost of maintaining the new pavilion (erected in 1970) proving a liability, a social secretary with ‘ideas and drive’ was required and Tiger stepped into the role in 1973.  He was aided by his great friend, Andrew Beach, and together they produced some superb social evenings including Black Country Nights, Disco’s, Themed Food evenings etc.   During a night of members’ entertainment, an act that had the audience in hysterics featured Andy Beach perched on the knee of Graham Williamson, in the style of ventriloquist Peter Brough and his puppet Archie Andrews.

A summer barbecue very nearly ended in disaster when it was decides that a pig would be barbecued. A pig was procured; a spit with an electric motor was constructed from a series of scrap components; scaffolding was erected alongside the pavilion to be covered with a tarpaulin in the event of rain.  Tiger impaled the pig on the spit and lit the barbecue at 5am on Saturday morning.  He soon found that he needed to raise the level of the barbecue coals to get more heat to the pig.  The barbecue process was continually interrupted by lack of fuel and rain.  At about 7pm in the evening the pig’s skin was crisp but the meat underneath was still raw and Tiger was very worried.  An Australian, trying to be helpful, prodded the crisp skin and a spurt of hot fat descended onto the hot barbecue.  Flames ascended the stream of fat and within microseconds the pig became a fireball.  The flames burned away the protective tarpaulin canopy and the pig was cooked.  The evening was rescued; although some people did complain about the lack of crackling and the overcooked meat!
With his organisational skills noted, he was persuaded to take on the role of the Clubs’ General Secretary in 1982 and he was elected a Life Member in 2008.

It is worth noting that Tiger became a very useful hockey player, playing in SCHC’s social 4th team and the Veterans’ side.  He played at centre forward, a position he held in his home-town soccer team.  Not having been taught hockey at school, he lacked many of the ‘finer’ skills and played a somewhat ‘robust’ game, but once inside the ‘D’ he wanted to shoot; he could hit the ball hard and he knew where the goalposts were.

entries.heading: Mark Rogers
paras: Mark was a product of Bishop Vesey Grammar School joining the Club as schoolboy, playing in the August holiday games.  In the 1978 season Mark featured in a second wicket stand of 154 for the Hawks at home to Tipton with David Stokes (102 runs) leaving Mark not out on 69.  Later that season Mark scored 108 not out for the 2nd team away at Newport.  In 1981 now in the 1st team opening the batting with Michael Dixon on Sundays he shared an opening partnership of 101, scoring 33 runs to Michael’s 63.  The records show later that season, that Mark scored 104 runs but it’s not clear who the 1st team opposition was, but in the 1984 season Mark with limited availability finished top of the 1st team averages having scored 386 runs at an average of 42.9, only batting on 11 occasions and was not out on 2.  One of the occasions was at Solihull when Mark opened the batting with James Ross scored 110 not out in their partnership of 128, which James contributing 46.  In the 1984 and 1985 seasons Mark figured in many centuries’ partnership with several games coming to mind, against strong opposition; Olton & WW 105 opening partnership with Chris Barber and later in the season with Graham Williamson against Knowle & Dorridge in a 166-run 2nd wicket partnership scoring 65 to Graham’s 91 runs.  Mark was not only a chartered accountant but was a very serious drummer in his band.

entries.heading: James M. Ross - Life Member
paras: James Ross turned up as a 15-year-old Repton schoolboy in 1970 on the recommendation of Norman Sharp to play for the for Sutton Grasshoppers who were all out for 71 chasing Nuneaton 121 runs on the Lower Ground.  James batted at No. 4 scored 3 runs. He did however have a bowl and took 1 for 23, but John Whyles took 5 for 9 runs.  However back at school he was in the Repton first team 1971 -73 and in his last year James scored 720 runs including two centuries in successive innings.  As a result, he was selected as reserve batsman for the Public Schools v the Indian Schools.

Although James had a great school record at Repton and as a pure batsman he was competing for a first team place against some exceptional cricketers. Bloomer, Dixon, Houghton, Barber, Gardom, McDowell, Jameson and Robinson and even in the second
Team there were many qualities player knocking on the 1st team door like Edmunds and Catt as well as ex-first team players stepping down as was the case of Pritchett.

James had to work extremely hard on his game playing in the twos in 1975, 76 and 77 scoring on average over 500 runs per season and in 1979 his capability to score runs with an aggregate total of 745 runs for the season was finally recognised so in the 1980 season James was an automatic 1st team player and confirmed his ability with a total of 1,003 runs in the season.

James had also established himself as the team opening batsman maintained a 1st team ever present player for the next 5 season when unfortunately, the club records for 1986 onwards were not maintained.

entries.heading: James Ross
paras: However, from another source of information James played 926 games for SCCC over 32 seasons with over 50% being with the 1st team.  As a 1st team player, he featured in 13 century partnerships of which 6 were in the first team sharing an opening partnership of 173 with Chris Barber.  During James's career, he scored 6 centuries in the 2nd Xl of which two not out centuries were 106 against K&D in 1976 and 111 against Halesowen.  His 1st Xl century was also against K&D in 1983 where James scored 113 runs.  He also managed to scored 30 fifties in 1st X1, 41 fifties in 2nd team 1 fifty with the Hawks and one fifty in the Club’s Sutton Schoolboys games.

James on leaving school still managed to play cricket for the Repton Pilgrims C.C. represented them in the Cricketer Cup competition appearing in the final in 1985 and scored a century in the first round of the competition in that season.  James still maintains his involvement with Repton Pilgrims Cricket Club and is their current President in the 2017-18 seasons.

Outside James’ playing career, he has held every major office in the Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club, initially as Treasurer in 1983 and 84, and then in 1990/1/2 & 3 he was Secretary.  A short break and in 1998 he was elected Chairman, a post he led for the next 4 years and in 2008 he took on the mantle of the Presidency of Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club a post he still holds today in 2017, however he also took back the chairmanship in 2009 for one year.  In 1995 the Club bestowed on James “Life Member of the Club” and in 2002 he was honoured by the Midland Club Cricket Conference as a “Cricketer of the Year”.  This award was followed in 2010 by James being elected a Vice President of the Birmingham & District Premier Cricket League.

entries.heading: J. Roy
paras: Justin Roy was a hard-hitting batsman and, on the hockey, pitch he was devastating with his powerful shots on goal.  However, in 1990 playing for the Hawks he routed Solihull with a fine spell of bowling, taking 7 wickets for 50 runs.  Later in the season he had 5 wickets haul on two other occasions.

entries.heading: R.E. Smith
paras: Ron as he was affectionately call, made his name as Chairman of the Club for four years, 1976 to 1979 inclusive.  In fact, he was the 1st Chairman to serve a 4-year term and only the Club’s 5 Chairman since the office was instigated in 1976 when H.A. Couchman was asked to run all meetings.  Prior to 1967, meetings were conducted by the President.  Ron did however play cricket but the only reference recorded about Ron’s playing career with the Sutton Club was in 1975 when playing for the 2nd Xl he took 7 wickets for 44 runs against Solihull, so he must have been a pretty good player.

entries.heading: David Stokes
paras: David first played for the Club as a 15-year-old playing along with his father, Barry in the Grasshoppers on a Sundays in 1976 where he scored 279 runs at an average of 23.3. However, he came to providence when he captained the Alpine Under-16 side in 1977 as a very promising opening batsman and in the 2nd team where he was the runner up to Roger Coombs, scoring 532 runs at an average of 20.5.  This resulted in David being awarded the Alec Hastilow Trophy as the “Best Under 16 Cricketer” by the MCCC.

In 1978 David again scored over 500 runs (598) at an average of 21.4.  The Club records are not clear when David played in the 1st team, as in 1980 season he played 10 games for the 2nd team with an average of 28, although he opened the batting with Michael Dixon in the 1st team.  He was unfortunately struck on the head by a ball that lifted of a length causing David to play as the first Sutton 1st team player wearing a helmet8

entries.heading: G. Stonier
paras: Graham Stonier joined the Club in the 1974 season and played in the 2nd team for the two seasons.  He was a big accumulator of runs and in his 1st season he scored 540 runs at an average of 27.0 and in the following season he scored 673 runs with a 30.6 average.  Graham scored 2 not out centuries in 1974 with 113 at home to Stratford and in the following season he scored 100 away at Solihull.  He also shared in 4 century partnerships as an opening batsman, one was of an un-broken 3rd wicket partnership with Chris Maynard of 135 runs, of which Graham scored 84 and Chris 50.

entries.heading: P. Sutcliffe
paras: Phil joined the Sutton Club in 1990, when he moved from Lancashire to work in Birmingham as a colleague of James Ross. As a left-hand batsman and right arm medium pace bowler he quickly established a permanent place in the first team as a run machine, scoring 110 runs at home against Harborne and in the game away at Bedworth, Phil, opened the batting and carried his bat on 74 not out when Sutton were bowled out for 175 chasing 276.  He also scored 80 against Mosley Ashfield and 80 not out against Halesowen, finishing top of the batting averages.  Unfortunately, no further records of Phil’s cricket performances with the Sutton Club although it is believed he left the Midlands in 1991 or 92

entries.heading: A.J. Sutton
paras: Adrian Sutton joined the Club from the Kings Heath Cricket Club when he moved house to live in Sutton in about 1993 and his cricketing abilities were well known and he immediately played for the 1st team and in 1995 he was elected their captain.  Although he was a very capable batsman, he was a quality bowler and was quickly among the wickets and in June that year he took 5 wickets for 36 runs and against Leamington and 5 for 44 against Olton.  Adrian was a very good administrator taking on the role of the Club’s General Secretary in 1994 and six years, although he had stopped playing long before 1999 as his family commitments required more of his attention.

entries.heading: Grahame Tidy
paras: Grahame - older brother to Warwick - for several seasons opening batsman / wicket-keeper in the 3rd. XI, entered the 1st team initially as a pace bowler / deep fieldsman who could bat. For many seasons, with so many quality team all-rounders, Grahame usually batted at No. 7, rather than playing in the 2nd team.  Back in the day, when players did not dive or slide around to prevent boundaries, he was a very good fielder (with Desperate Dan stride and siege-gun throw), without the need to rack up dry-cleaning bills! With so many spinners in the team, Beach, Gardom, Warwick and Torry, a safe pair of hands on the square leg / mid-wicket boundary was highly rewarding to the bowling attack.

Most of Grahame’s runs scored in the 1st team were when the stars had failed (very often he was at the crease with five wickets down for fewer than fifty on the board); so, Grahame was required to graft, and he shared a number of century partnerships batting at No.7.  One comes to mind against Barnt Green in 1975 with a 108 runs partnership with Chris Maynard, 81 not out, and with Grahame out for 23. In the 1978 August bank holiday Tuesday fixture against Aldridge, given the opportunity to open the batting by skipper, Keith Gardom, Grahame scored a century at Rectory Park. In his early days, playing as a pace bowler in the 1st team, in 1971 he finished second to his brother in the aggregate and averages with 52 wickets and an average of 23. Grahame was a regular tourist with the Mayflies CC to the Gliffaes Country Hotel to play against the local cricket teams in the surrounding area.

entries.heading: Warwick Tidy
paras: Warwick Nigel Tidy was born 10 February 1953 in Sutton Coldfield and went to the then John Willmott Grammar School and at the age of 15, Warwick joined  SCCC whilst still at School and played initially in the 2nd Xl, a right hand batsman who bowled leg breaks and googlies.  By the start of the 1970 season Warwick was a regular 1st team player for Warwickshire CCC (being the third youngest ever to make a Championship debut at just 17) and he also played just one List “A” match for Warwickshire against Middlesex
in the John Players Sunday League competition, which was televised. He played for the County until 1974 and was a member of their County Championship winning side of

entries.heading: Warwick N. Tidy
paras: 1972.  He played on 36 occasions for his County taking 81 wickets at 34.25 with a best of 5 wickets for 24 runs

As a school boy of 15-16 years of age he maintained a remarkable control of his leg breaks and googlies which were bowled at a lively pace, and throughout his school days he played most weekends in the Sutton 1st Xl obtaining more than fifty wickets.in the 1969 season. On being released by the County, Warwick rejoined the Sutton club and took 81 wickets for 16.35 and again in 1977 he took 69 wickets at 15.07 before leaving the Midlands to take up an appointment in Plymouth, Devon as a building society manager before branching out to run his own mortgage brokers business.  However Warwick continued playing club cricket for Plymouth Cricket Club in the "A" Division of the Devon Cricket League between 1979 and 1987 still bowling his leg breaks and googlies.

entries.heading: D. Torry
paras: Dave joined the Club in 1977 from Streetly as a very tall left arm spin bowler averaging over 50 wickets a season at an average of 18.0 runs per wicket before he left the UK to take up an engineering post in Africa

In 1982 he took 6 for 67 against Coventry & NW and 5 for 28 runs against Aston Unity.   Dave played a number of games for the Warwickshire County 2nd Xl and was a competitive tourist with the Warwickshire Pilgrims.

entries.heading: Brian Turner
paras: Brian joined the Club around 1971and became a stalwart in the Hawkes & Grasshoppers teams dominating their batting throughout the 5 seasons he played and took over the captaincy of the Hawks in 1973 - 4 & 5 finishing top of both teams batting aggregates and averages most seasons, scoring some 3,299 runs for the Club with an average of 30 runs per innings.  Brian in the 1975 season scored a combined total of 1,045 runs for the Hawks and Grasshoppers.  1,000 runs in a season was a rarely achieved in lower ground cricket.  Brian generally opened the batting and figured in 6 century partnerships with the most unlikely colleagues and had a 137-run 1st wicket partnership in 1975 with a J. Chambers for the Grasshoppers against Hampton in Arden scoring 85 runs when the partnership was broken.

entries.heading: Peter Yates
paras: Peter was born in 1930 and was educated at Bishop Vesey Grammar School before being called up to do National Service with the RAF as a corporal in the Military Police at RAF Honington, Nr. Thetford, Suffolk; the home of RAF Transport Command.  Returning to civilian life Peter joined Streetly Cricket Club, where his father was an active member which was before that Club moved to Briar Avenue.  After meeting up with Norman Sharp, Peter moved his allegiance to the Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club in 1951 when P.P. Ashcroft invited him to play with the first team as a left arm quick bowler, who could also bat when needed.
Peter played for the 1st Xl for the next 25 years, bowling up the slop in Rectory Park before he called it a day after the 1976 season.

In 1953 Peter took 47 wickets at an average of 23.5 runs per wicket. During the 25 years Peter averaged between 35 and 50 wickets a season with an average in the late teens.  However, he did have many purple patches like a hat trick when at home to Burton, removing their batsmen No’s. 2, 3 & 4 and then at away the Aston Unity ground in Court Lane he had the distinction of taking 8 for 27 runs in 10.3 overs for an average of 3.4 runs per wicket.  With so much bowling talent available to the many Sutton captains, Peter’ opportunities were limited, in particular as they had 6 ft. 6, left arm spinner Les Pellow taking 100 wickets a season, and Neil Houghton doing likewise. However, during a period of 16 consecutive seasons between, 1953 and 1968 the Clubs record have recorded that Peter took 450 wickets at a cost of just over 17.5 runs per wicket. He finished top of the averages in 1956 and 57 and finish most season in the top 3 bowlers.  Peter did play a few games in the 2nd Xl taking 91 wickets at an average of just under 14 runs per wicket

Peter could bat, but again his opportunities were few, again due to the number of quality batsmen that played for Sutton during the fifties & sixties.  Although batting at No. 8 he had a number of 7 wicket record partnerships that were close to a hundred runs.

Having now retired from playing Peter in 1977 took up golf as well as putting together a group of youngsters to play in the Under-16 cricket league.  This was a new concept for junior cricket and in the role of manager of the youngster they won the local league, then the area knock-out competition, before going on to win the Under-16 Alpine Soft Drinks Competition. These games were all 20 over a side game in the evening for the initials rounds and then on Moseley Cricket Club ground for the semi-finals and final which Sutton young team won, beating Wolverhampton and Leamington in the semi-final and final respectively.

Peter was also the Club’s secretary in 1971 and 1972, and today at the age of 88 he still continues to support and retain his membership with the Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club after 66 seasons - a fine achievement by a great player and loyal member.
2000 A New Millennium

entries.heading: Paul Greetham
paras: At the AGM of 2000, Adrian Sutton stood down as the club’s secretary with Paul Greetham taking on this important roll but relinquished the Sunday captaincy of the 1st Team in favour of Richard Dandy.  The only other changes were David Taylor moving from the captaincy of the Grasshoppers to the Hawks with Andy Thomas taking on the Grasshoppers job.
Francois van de Merve, from South African was engaged as our overseas player

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: An annual dinner was held at Aston Wood Golf Club on Friday 28th January with Fred Truman OBE, Yorkshire C.C.C. and England 1952 to 1965 speaking about his life in cricket and in the Northern Clubs as an entertainer, The presentation of club awards and prizes were made by both the President, Peter Wells and Mr F.S. Trueman OBE.
1st Team results in 2000

The 1st team had a good season in the 1st division of the B&DPCL with four batsmen producing some good performances with Jon Ship scoring a total of 527 runs with an average of 28.2 and a highest score of 93.  He was closely followed by Richard Dandy with an aggregate total 494 runs with an average of 29.1 and a highest score of 193 not out.  The other two runs’ contributors were Louis Aspelling with 443 aggregate total of runs with an average of 27.7 and Paul Smith (released by Warwickshire C.C.C.) with 419 runs to his credit and an average of 26.2.  In the bowling, R. East took 58 wickets at a cost of 19.12 runs per wicket

entries.heading: Gaz Durrani
paras: A Memorable Game and the award of the Robert Atherton K.O. Trophy Cup Winners to the Sunday 2nd Team who travelled to play against Coventry & N.W. Cricket 2nd team in the final.

Having arrived at the Binley Road ground it was clear to all that there was no possible of any play as it had rained all day and a bowl-out was impossible.   With neither side being able to agree on a replay date, it was agreed that the face of a coin would determine the result.  The Coventry captain tossed the coin and the person, Gaz Durrani, who had travelled the furthest, would make the call.  Gaz called correctly so Sutton were declared the winners and won the trophy without a ball being.  So “Sutton won by a Distance”

entries.heading: Ken Lancaster 2001
paras: This AGM was a very quiet affair with only a couple of changes in the captains in the lower sides.  On Saturday the 2nd team would be captained by Ken Lancaster and on a Sunday the 2nd Xl captain would be Dave Taylor replacing James Ross and Naeem Arif respectively.  The Hawks and Grasshoppers would remain in the hands of Dave and Andy.

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: An annual dinner was held at Aston Wood Golf Club on Friday 26th January with Geoff Miller, Derbyshire C.C.C., Essex C.C.C. Natal and England who proposed a toast to the Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club.  Geoff as an England Test selector gave an insight in to the difficulties in selecting players to go on overseas tours.  The President Peter Wells, assisted by James Ross and Geoff Miller presented a number of awards.

entries.heading: Ship & Randall
paras: In a 45 over KO game away against Barnt Green, J. Ship opened the batting and scored 109 runs when the innings closed at 217 for 8. In reply Barnt Green closed at 215 for 9 wickets leaving Sutton the winners by 2 runs. In a match home to Aston Unity, Randall opened the batting and scored 126 out of a total of 241 when the Sunday League of 45 overs closed. In reply Unity were all bowled out for 39 runs in 15 overs.

entries.heading: Bobby Arif  & Abdul Raqib
paras: In a Warwickshire Sunday League game which is limited to 40 over per side, Sutton scored 365 for 8 wickets declared at Griff & Cotton2nd Xl game; Bobby Arif 165 not out and Abdul Raqib 114, with a partnership of 156 runs in 18 overs.   In another WSL game Sutton at home against Kings Heath scored 340 runs for the loss of 6 wickets, with Bilal Aziz 212.
Bobby scored 510 runs in the season at an average of 51.0, including a second hundred against Kenilworth.

entries.heading: Mike Hepburn
paras: The Club through the SCC&HC L agree a new 30-year ground lease covering 3.33 hectares is signed on 25th December 2001 with Birmingham City Council, at a charge of £3,000 per annum payable in advance by 4 equal payments per quarter day reviewable upwards every 5 years

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: At the 2002 AGM, James Ross who had been Chairman since 1998 stood down and was duly thanked by the President for his years of service.  Nigel Lyon was elected the Club’s Chairman, with Michael Dean being elected treasurer in place of Hugo Russell and was also thanked for his years of service.

Richard Dandy took over the Saturday 1st Team captaincy from Jon Miller and retaining the Sunday captaincy with Bobby Arif becoming the 2nd Team Saturday captain and A. Raqib being responsible for the Sunday team and Steve Budd becoming the Hawkes new captain.

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: An annual dinner was again held at Aston Wood Golf Club on Friday 25th January2002 with Gladstone Small, Warwickshire C.C.C. & England stepping in at the last minute for Chris Cowdrey.  Our President, Peter Wells proposed a toast to our Guests which Gladstone gave a very interesting reply.
Waquas Chugtai,

The Club also engaged Waquas Chugtai, an 18-year-old fast bowler from Pakistan as our overseas player but because of his age the league rules prevents him bowling as much as we would have liked. Rob Cuncliffe from Leicestershire C.C.C. was released to play for us when not required by L.C.C.C. and Paul Smith, Ex Warwickshire C.C.C. also joined us.

entries.heading: The M.C.C.C. elected James Ross “Cricketer of the Year”
paras: Richard Dandy wins the 1st Xl 2nd Division Warwickshire Sunday League player of the year award. The 2nd Team win the Division 2 cup K.O. against Kenilworth.
Bobby Arif 2nd Saturday Xl Captain took 7 for 18 runs in 23 overs bowling Pelsall C.C. out for 112 runs in reply to Sutton’s modest total of 136.
The Under 13 Xl was the Group Winners of the Warwickshire Cricket Board.

entries.heading: Neil Houghton
paras: The AGM was rather a quiet affair with only changes in captaincy mainly in the 2nd team with both Bobby Arif, and A. Raqib standing down as Saturday and Sunday captains and were replaced by Jimmy Little and M Ahmed respectively.  The Grasshoppers also had a new captain in A. Hatch.  The
President was pleased to announce that W.N. (Neil) Houghton, had been elected Chairman of the Warwickshire County Cricket Club, a post he holds until 2010
The Association of the joint clubs was re-organised, with the Cricket Club taking over full responsibility for the ground maintenance.  The Club acquired its first set of roll on roll off covers.

entries.heading: Peter Wells
paras: Aston Wood Golf Club had now become the venue for the Club’s Annual Dinner and on Friday 31st January 2003 close to 100 members and guests attended.  Richard Sperryn being invited to say grace, which he did, in his did in his now customary humorous but respectful manner.  Peter Wells proposed a toast to our guests and the Hon Christopher Cowdrey, Kent C.C.C., Glamorgan C.C.C. & England, responded apologising for having to withdraw twelve months earlier.

entries.heading: Victor Walker-Randall
paras: Although three players in the 1st Team had outstanding performances, they did not prevent the Club being relegated for the 1st Division in the Birmingham & District Premier League at the end of the season.  The club had engaged Victor Walker-Randall, a South African as our over-seas player who scored scores 515 runs in the Saturday league side.  Richard Dandy also scored over 500 runs, just making it with 505 runs.  Michael Dean took 48 league wickets.
However, as conciliation, the 1st Team won the Warwickshire Sunday league Division 1 Championship which they shared with the Harborne Cricket Club, but lost in the cup final to Nuneaton.
The Sutton Sunday 2nd Xl won to retain the Division 2 cup with a victory in the final over Olton & W.W.C.C.
The 3rd Team won the West Midlands North Division Club Cricket League Championship.

entries.heading: Obituary to Graham Williamson
paras: All members were saddened at the sudden death of Graham Williamson on the 19th July 2003 at his home in Knowle following being stung by a bee while mowing the lawn a few days earlier.  Graham had joined the Club in 1983 after graduating at Manchester University and became 1st team Saturday captain in 1985 and held both the Saturday and Sunday 1st Team captaincies.  Graham was a fast-scoring batsman, who also provided the impetus and support to boost the team with his hard-hitting style.  In 1983 he scored 637 runs on Saturdays with an average of 28.9 and his 106 not out won the game again against Olton.  Graham relinquished the captaincies in 1987 and left the area in 1989 joining Knowle & Dorridge C.C.  Graham was an excellent after dinner speaker and would always entertain his audience with his humor and did just that in the Club’s Annual Dinner in 2001.  His funeral in Knowle and afterwards at the K&D C.C. Clubhouse was well attended by Graham’s many friends in Sutton.  The B&DPCL instigated the Graham Williamson KO trophy, which is competed annual in Graham’s memory.  Graham left a widow Julie and two young sons.

entries.heading: Nigel Lyon
paras: Nigel Lyon stood down as the Club’s Chairman for which the President, Peter Wells thanked him for his years of service – (2 years) . John Howard a relative new member, who now resided in Sutton and had a considerable amount of club cricket management with the Halesowen Cricket Club and was duly elected as Chairman.  After a lengthy discussion and a vote regarding a new position of a Club Captain, who did not necessarily have to be a captain on the pitch and would play in whichever team his ability warranted it was unanimously agreed that Paul Greetham would be elected as the club’s first “Club Captain”.  The only other change in the Club’s officials was J-P Shannahan replacing Steve Budd as the Hawkes Captain.

It was announced that Tim Groenewald from South Africa, an all-rounder was to be engaged as our overseas player.  Incidentally Tim was taken on as a professional with Warwickshire C.C.C. before moving to Derbyshire C.C.C. and in 2015 joins Somerset C.C.C.

entries.heading: Neil Houghton
paras: Aston Wood Golf Club had now the venue for the Club’s Annual Dinner and on Friday 30th January and about 100 members and guests attended with Neil Houghton, now Chairman of Warwickshire County Cricket Club saying grace.  Peter Wells gave an interesting prologue on our guest speakers’ cricketing career from Natal C.C, Hampshire C.C.C. and England of Robin Smith, who finished his address with a toast to the Sutton Club.
Ode to the Last Safe

entries.heading: By Peter Bell
paras: I have closed my door for the very last time
after fifty years in the prevention of crime,
looking after the club's Brandy, Gin, Whisky, and Wine
kept within my steel body for short periods of time.
My door was always opened with care and attention
using a long key to penetrate my internal dimension,
I would respond with a loud click to certify my intention
of opening my steel door with the minimum of stimulation.
Villains, with an electrical grinder, gave me a terrible fright
when they attacked my body in the middle of the night.

entries.heading: ignoring the fact, that I am 5 tons in weight and six feet in height
paras: and built in the late nineteenth century, long before the era of flight.
I had served Midland Bank for over sixty years with distinction,

entries.heading: retiring in the sixties to watch Sutton play cricket as a relaxation
paras: Last week, when attacked I was thrown on my back, without any consideration
so, arrangements were made for me to become a totally new creation.
I have now been uplifted and shipped to a steel plant in Chin'er!
to be smelted and rolled, into either a cheap new bar shutter,
or to be sold by Ratners to those awful villains as crap or clutter,
like a fork that bends and a knife that won't cut butter.

entries.heading: Annual General Meeting 2005
paras: This year’s AGM produced a number of changes to the committee with Ken Lancaster becoming secretary, Simon Newby taking over the treasures position, from Paul Greetham and Michael Dean respectively.  Richard Dandy relinquished the 1st Team Sunday captain in favour of Dan Davis, but retained the Saturday captain’s position. J-P Shannahan stood down as the Hawkes captain in favour of Mirza Ahmed.  Paul Greetham was reelected as Club Captain.
Tim Groenewald, returns for a second season as our overseas player and is offered a 2-year contract with Warwickshire C.C.C.

entries.heading: The Groundsman’s Shed
paras: After many years, and probably due to a lack of maintenance aided by vandals who would climb on to its roof, it collapsed.

entries.heading: Birmingham Sports Council Award
paras: The Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club was declared Sports Club of the Year on Friday 25th February 2005 at the Birmingham Sports Council Awards evening at the NIA.

The Club was nominated by the Warwickshire County Cricket Club, and beat a short list of five, which included Birchfield Harriers Athletics Club.  The outgoing Chairman, Nigel Lyon, and, current Chairman, John Howard, were delighted with the award.  John said: “This reflects the tremendous effort, dedication and team spirit over the past five years which has gone into improving and offering the best in all respects to cricketers of all ages.”

The award finishes a successful season, both on and off the field.  On the playing, side, the 1st XI won the Birmingham. Premier League Division 2 and were joint Winners of the Warwickshire Sunday league Division 1.

entries.heading: The under-13 and under-15 teams won their respective county championships
paras: Off the field, Sutton Coldfield became the first club in "Birmingham to achieve the ECB Clubmark award, which recognizes quality coaching for junior members in a totally friendly and safe environment. Sutton is also a Focus Club designated by the Warwickshire County Cricket Board.

John added: "The Clubmark award is the culmination of some extremely hard work, by several members of the club. "Praise must go to Eric Harding (club administrator) and Colin Greetham (chairman, junior section), for their time, devotion and determination in helping achieve this award." Winter nets are well under way and outdoor nets start on 14th April for senior playing members and 16th April for juniors.  The club is also taking part in Cricket Force. (A combination of Changing Rooms painting and Ground Force teams working on the ground) during the weekend of April 2 and 3.

The project is a community initiative centered on the cricket club whereby local businesses and people from the community are invited to spend time and donate materials, labour or any appropriated resources to renovate the facilities.

Sutton is also seeking active partners in the community and within local businesses to help take the club further forward with its development plan.  The award was well covered by the local newspaper “The Sutton Coldfield News”

entries.heading: Memorial Bench
paras: The club was presented with 6-foot teak bench on Wednesday 20th May 05, by the Captain’s Mother, Lynda Dandy in memory of her late father Don Thornton, who prior to his illness had been a regular supporter watching his grandson Richard Dandy grow up while developing his cricket ability to become 1st Team captain.  Unfortunately, the bench was stolen the next day and never recovered, despite a reward being offered by the Sutton Coldfield News, in their weekly paper out on Friday 29th May under a title: -
Reward for Stolen Memorial Bench.

entries.heading: By Nick McCarthy
paras: Heartless thieves have stolen a memorial bench from Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club, which was only delivered last week. The club, which is based -on Rectory Road, is demanding that people “spare a thought for the man” it honoured and they have since offered a substantial reward for information that leads to its recovery. The six-foot teak bench, presented by the family of the late Don Thornton, a distinctive inscription “In memory of Don - he was happy here."

Don, grandfather of first team captain Richard Dandy, had spent many weekends watching games before his death in January. His daughter, Linda Dandy, told the News that she and-her family were devastated with the theft and were now preparing to break the news to mother. She added “I did not think people would do this kind of thing. They may have tried to sell it, but it looks like a memorial bench and we just hope that somebody can contact the club or the police with information.

entries.heading: Scandalous
paras: "We had only sat on the bench once and now it is gone. Watching Richard play cricket was one of the few things my father could do as he got older and it is just very sad for all of us." Club Spokesman, Peter Bell, described the incident as scandalous and he said the club was determined to recover the bench. He added: "During last year's cricket season one of our memorial benches was taken by vandals and was used to mike a fire in the woods in Rectory Park. “This latest theft, of another memorial bench, shows more callous disregard for people's feelings. "The family presented the bench for the

entries.heading: Gwen Thornton & her Son, Tony
paras: benefit of all who wish to enjoy the beauty of Rectory Park and we plan to replace it."
Anybody with. information on the theft, which happened sometime between (May 18) and Friday (May 20), can contact the club or can call police in Sutton CoIdfield on 0845 113 5000.

entries.heading: Obituary to Richard Sperryn
paras: Richard Sperryn, respectfully known as Dick, passed away in his sleep on the 23rd April 2006, age 63.  Members and friends of the Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club were deeply saddened to learn of Dick’s sudden death although not an outstanding cricketer he was an outstanding personality both on and off the cricket ground.  He was an excellent captain and deeply respected by all who played for or against the Hawks.

Dick was captain for three periods of time, the first occasion was for three years1968 to 1970 but for health warnings he did not play cricket, so he umpired the 1st Team Sunday games for the 1972 and 1973 seasons, but retuned to captain the Hawks in 1977 for a further three seasons, but stood down in 1980 only to return for the 1981 season by demand by all players in the 3rd team games.

Searching through the batting records Dick’s name does not appear very often, but he was a regular with the 1st team on the Bank Holiday games against Aldridge and even captained the side on one occasion.  He did have a couple of games in the 1st Team, when a very late cry off necessitated Dick being called upon as a late replacement at Harborne Cricket Club, where captain Michael Dixon invited Dick to open the batting with himself, Dick scored a very quick 22 runs before being dismissed.

I can also recall, when I was umpiring in one of the last games played on the old Bromsgrove Cricket Club ground, before Bryant’s built houses on the land, that both Dick and Charles Groves being seconded from the Hawks to join the 1st Team just before they were departing for Bromsgrove, due to sudden domestic emergency involving two of the 1st Team players.  After the fall of the 8th wicket both Dick and Charles were batting together, but as neither having scored a run and both very anxious to get off the mark the inevitable happened with calls of “Yes” by both batsmen quickly followed by “No’s” resulted in both batsmen being at the same end and Dick was judged to be “Run Out”.  His departing words to Charles were, “You have had all season to run me out with the Hawks, why wait until we are in the 1st Team before doing so”.

Dick was a true club man prepared to play to the best of his ability for whichever team he played.  As a captain his very strong personality, charisma and enthusiasm producing the best out of the young players that surrounded him.  He taught them how to win and how to lose with dignity and respect for their opposition.

Not only was Dick an outstanding captain he was an excellent after dinner speaker and spoke on eight occasions at the Club’s Annual Dinner, either replying to a toast to the Club or to propose a toast to the guests.  At many dinners Dick was asked to say grace which he did in a carefully prepared monologue taking into account the occasion for the dinner, he introduced wit and humor, yet still retaining a certain amount of reverence for the occasion although it was limited at times.

Dick was an excellent administrator and was President of the joint cricket and hockey clubs.  He was the instigator of the development of the Aston Unity & Spartan Rugby Football Club’s ground becoming the rugby club’s President and a trustee.  His interest and enthusiasm for both sports were developed in his school days at Bromsgrove School.

He was an excellent tourist and for over 25 years he went with the Mayflies Cricket Club on their annual visit to Wales to stay a week at the Gliffaes Country House Hotel in Crickhowell to play cricket against the local Crickhowell Club side, and a day games at Builth Wells C.C. and Abergavenny C.C. and on one occasion the local side played Malcolm Nash of Gary Sobers fame against the Mayflies, resulting in Dick injuring a finger and visiting Abergavenny Hospital.

entries.heading: Obituary to Terry Matthews
paras: Terry Matthews, an interesting, entertaining and sometime controversial person died suddenly on 23rd December 2008 at home in Crown Lane at the age of 72, or as Terry proudly preferred, B73.  “Tel” as he became known to his friends, arrived in Sutton Coldfield in 1989 when he left South Staff Social Services.  He had been their spokesman and a person we had observed in that role on Midlands Television.  Terry’s early days playing cricket was with Whitmore Cricket Club, but he soon made an impact on both Sutton 3rd teams as very jovial and enthusiastic slow right arm bowler relying on flight and length rather than spin.

In 1991 and 1992 Terry was elected vice captain of both the Hawks and Grasshoppers teams and in 1993 and 1994 he captained both teams but relinquished the Hawks job in 1995 and the Grasshoppers position in 1997, but became the vice-captain of both teams again until 2003 when he retired from playing the game he so much enjoyed.  The highlight of his captaincy the Hawks were winners of the Willis Corroon M.C.C.C. 3rd Xl League, which he was immensely proud.   Not many records are retained by the 3rd teams except that Terry took a total of 43 wickets in the 1990 season for 847 runs at a cost of 19.7 & on 3 occasions took 5 wickets.

One of Terry’s great attributes was his ability to tell a good story and he was never afraid to relate a situation where he was the “fall guy”.  Terry had a glass eye and there were many stories about that, but this story relates to the opening of the M6 Toll Road which Terry decided to try it out.  With the exact change in his hand, he took his car through the automatic fast unmanned payment booth just like the cars in front and those following, the cash is tossed into the collecting receptacle.  Nothing can go wrong except Terry missed the bin and having no other change he had to get out and go under his car to retrieve the funds, unfortunately it was raining and this fast procedure of payment resulted in a big queue of cars hooting their car horns as Terry grovelled looking for his cash.

Terry will be sadly missed by his many senior friends, affectionately known as the “Golden Oldies” spending a Saturday evening in the bar enjoying a drink and listening to Terry’s many yarns.  They were basically what Terry had done in the last week working for a local firm of solicitors, investigating possible compensation claims as a result of an accident whereby negligence may have been the cause.  This resulted in Terry get his leg pulled any time the sound of an ambulance was heard, but Terry could always turn the tide on the author of such remarks with a humorous response.

Terry always had a very helpful attitude towards junior players that played in the Hawks and Grasshopper teams that he, as captain, giving them every opportunity to take an active part in the game so that they were able to be promoted into the senior club sides.  His Family through his son, Simon presented the Club with a Memorial Board to acknowledge a junior player who had during the season showed great promise, improvement and progressed in his cricketing skills.  The Terry Matthews Junior Award was first awarded at the end of the 2009 season by the end of 2014 every annual recipient had played 1st Team cricket and one was now earning a living as a professional cricketer with the Warwickshire County Cricket Club.  How proud Terry would have been.

entries.heading: Obituary to Peter Wells
paras: The Club was saddened to learn that their immediate Past President, Peter Wells had passed away in March 2009 in Clitheroe, following an accident in his new home.  Peter who had three main interests in life, his teaching, cricket and his love of art in particular water colour painting.

Peter was born in Erdington and went to the local junior school before passing the grammar school entrance exam into Saint Philips Grammar School at the Oratory in Birmingham, after which he went to the Birmingham Art College, obtaining a Bachelor of Art.  He then took up an English teaching post at Saints Mary and John Catholic Primary School, Birmingham, later to become the school’s Head Teacher before taking on the headship of a large school in Warley, on the other side of Birmingham.

Peter joined the Sutton club in 1949 as a 17-year-old having just left school and continued playing into the 1990’s, he was a medium to fast quick right arm bowler who had a deceptive turn of pace which surprised a lot of batsmen, for which he was known affectingly as “Seam”.  Playing in one of his first games for the 2nd Xl team at the Bishop Vesey Grammar School he took 6 school wickets for 11runs in 12 overs of which 6 were maidens.  However, his most outstanding bowling performance was in the 1st Team against Leicester Ivanhoe in 1963 at Rectory Park, Peter took 6 wickets for 14 runs in 16 overs, although his 6 wickets for 7 runs for the 2nd Xl away against Bromsgrove in 1968 was a match winning performance and incidentally two seasons earlier he had a hat trick on the same ground.  This was not Peter’s first hat trick he had achieved this distinction in 1958 against Pickwick Nomads.  Peter played cricket in the 1st and later in the 2nd team for 20 seasons before dropping down to play and captain both the Hawks and Grasshoppers at various times, although he had a continuous period of 6 seasons, 1970 to 1975 as the Grasshoppers captain.  Peter concluded his playing days as captain of the Hawks in 1976 putting on the white coat to umpire whenever a club side was short of an umpire.

In 1962 Peter took up the organization of the Mayflies Cricket Club annual visit to Wales, staying a week at the Gliffaes Country House Hotel in Crickhowell to play cricket against the local cricket club sides.  This organisation required matching accommodation and players touring and opposition from local club sides including Crickhowell C.C, Abergavenny C.C and a day-game against Builth Wells C.C. These three clubs were the mainstay of the tour with two other sides being found annually.  In Peter in his early days as a tourist he played daily, but as he moved into later years, he would play an odd game and would score or umpire as the matches demanded.

Peter realised that clubs needed to produced their own experienced young players to join the seniors sides when they were able to cope with long duration and highly competitive games, so sometime in the late 1960’s Peter started to organize some competitive cricket for school boys so by 1974 he had a fixtures list established with like-minded clubs from Ashfield, Harborne and Moseley Cricket Clubs to play cricket over a two week period, on a home and away games basis during August.

Cricket Nets were introduced for boys between the ages of 12 to 18 years on every Friday evening at 6 PM during July and August, with all the details displayed in the Clubs fixture card as Colts Xl Fixtures.

By 1977 Peter had set up a fixture list of 9 games in three August weeks and introduced cricket to boys under 15 years of age who would play cricket on Sunday afternoons on Sutton’s lower ground in May and June, with Friday nets being available.  Peter had so much junior cricket organized he had to hand over the Alpine competition to Peter Yates to run.  Sutton success over many years with young players coming through to play 1st Team cricket was down to the foresight and organization by Peter.

One could not let pass without referring to Peter love of painting, for in his later years he would go out with likeminded friends to paint in water colour.  He also offered to paint a landscape view of the cricket ground which was accepted and signed print copies were sold to members to raise a much-needed income for the club.

Peter also had an exhibition of his work held in Lichfield Cathedral where he showed some 40 painting of both the inside and outside views of UK cathedrals which he presented to all Cathedral Deans for them to do what they wished.

Peter was elected on to the Club’s committee in 1967 and stayed on until he became Chairman in 1981, a post he held for four years and in 1983 Peter was elected a Life Member and in 1992 he became President, remaining the Club’s figurehead until he left the Midland in 2008, but died some 12 months later.

A memorial service was held in Saint Mary’s RC Church in Harborne in the June, which was very well attended by both Sutton members and his many friends.  From Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club’s view on Peter’s life, he was the originator of the need for coaching and introducing boys into the joy of playing cricket.

entries.heading: Neil Houghton
paras: Neil Houghton relinquishes the Chairmanship of Warwickshire C.C.C. a post he has held for 7 years - 2003 to 2010 having been their treasurer for 11 years - 1987 to 1998. During his Chairmanship of the County Club Neil oversaw the redevelopment of the Edgbaston ground for it to become one of the worlds, top test match arenas.  Neil had an outstanding playing career with Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club, Warwickshire CCC's 2nd Xl, the MCC and representing the Midland Club Cricket Conference on numerous occasions being elected Cricketer of the Year in 1961.

entries.heading: W.N. Houghton - The Administrator
paras: Neil was invited by the Warwickshire County Cricket Club in 1982, to represent Sutton Coldfield on the County Committee following the death of Arthur Spencer, who had been the area representative for a number of years.

As a Chartered Accountant, Neil was elected on the Club’s Catering Committee as their treasurer, his step on his way up the County club’s promotion ladder. His colleagues and palls back at the Sutton Coldfield Club were anything but respectful referring to “Neil being in charge of the pork pies or scotch eggs”. However, he did a good job and was elected the Club’s Honorable Treasure in 1987, a post he held for 12 years.

In 1999, Neil was elected Vice Chairman, before being elected Chairman in 2003. He held this post for 7 years, overseeing the development and modernizing of the Edgbaston ground, to be recognized as an international sports arena. Gone were the trapping of the old village pavilion of the pre second world war era. All you could say about the old façade was “It was good to look at” but became useless in the modern game of cricket. On a personal note, I remember the many occasions when umpiring at Edgbaston, the dressing room was a box room with no view of the ground.

National Administration

entries.heading: THE SUTTON COLDFIELD CRICKET CLUB REPORT FROM THE
MIDLANDS CLUB CRICKET CONFEENCE HANDBOOK FOR 2010
paras: Not a completely successful year for Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club, but it may have been worse, bearing in mind that there was almost a complete change of Captains, which always takes time for them to settle in, but there is an indication that this coming season will hold better promise. From the playing point of view, it was the Sunday Elevens that had the more profitable season, albeit, mainly only the Second XI.

Again, the Junior Sides played well within their own sphere, and made their presence felt with some good performances in the Senior Sides, this being a credit to all the managers and coaches, that put in so much time and effort to ensure the success that is attained.

There are several changes on the Administration side of the Club, Jamie Ross remains as President, but has relinquished the position of Chairman to Naeem Arif, who made a welcome return to the club in 2009, after not playing for a few seasons. Ken Lancaster continues as Secretary, but there is a change as to who is in charge of the purse-strings, with Adil Bhatti becoming Treasurer. The Chairpersons of the Committees are Cricket/ Selection, Mark Guest, Ground, Paul Heron, Juniors, Colin Greetham, and the newly formed Ladies Committee, Kim Harvey. We are indebted to Andrew Sargent, who continues to carry out his, dedicated duties, as the Club Web-Site Manager.

Captains in the main remain the same, First XI (Saturday), Mark Guest, Second XI (Saturday), Martin Ball, Third XI (Saturday), is taken over by Steve Russell, First XI (Sunday), Naeem Arif, who is promoted from the Second XI, he is replaced in the Second XI, by Simon Broadhead, Nigel Hornby continues in charge of the Third XI (Sunday).

The playing record was not, overall, very successful, the First XI (Saturday) were relegated for the second year running, and will be playing in the Third Division of the Birmingham & District Premier Cricket League, in the 2010 season. It was a difficult season for Mark Guest to take on in his first year as Captain, several experienced players became unavailable, which meant blooding young players into the side, and it was towards the end of the season before the side began show an improvement, at least this does give some encouragement for the next season. Considering the concerns for the Captaincy, Mark's own game was not affected too much, he scored over three hundred runs, but only had limited howling opportunities. Steve Booth, a newcomer to the club, made nearly four hundred runs, together with sixteen wickets, having started the season in the Second XI, unfortunately Steve will be unavailable to play in 2010.

Mike Dean was hampered by injuries, but was having a good season with the bat finishing with an average of 27.63, and taking a few wickets, sadly this may have been Mike's last season. Junior player, Jamie Mapper, continued to show promise with the bat, having an average of 25.20, at the end of the season. Others to have made contributions with the bat were, Sam Irvine, Matthew Parker and Graham Clark. Richard Norgrove was the top wicket-taker, finishing with thirty-four victims at an average of 18.44, the main support came from Andy Stevenson with twenty-five wickets and Steven Howard with twenty wickets, Nick Thompson always performed well when promoted from the Second XI. Mike Randall was the leading fielder, taking ten catches.

The Second XI (Saturday) started off in a similar fashion to the First XI, but, with some determination, and commitment, had a good second half of the season, finishing in fifth place in Division II, only just outside fourth place, and with a lot of promise for the 2010 season. Skipper, Martin Ball, did a good job in his first season, as Captain, taking twenty-five wickets at 18.64, and getting his side back on the right track, so leaving a sound basis on which to challenge for promotion in the coming season. Rob Day also did well with the ball, taking twenty-five wickets, in his first season back to the club. Nick Thompson could always be relied upon, when called into the attack, finishing with fourteen wickets, Stuart Russell also did well in taking nineteen wickets. The batting was well led by Jack Smith, who made well over three-hundred runs at an average of 56.67. Top score for the season, went to Chris Hobbis, who had a knock of 94 in his total of three hundred and five runs, whilst Tom Naraine's average of 26.67, came from his total of one-hundred and sixty runs that he made. Sam Elgar, one of the club's most promising Junior Players, scored over three-hundred runs, and batted most consistently, when opening the batting. Several of the players mentioned will stand the Second XI in good stead for next season, unless they are playing for the First XI.

The Third XI (Saturday) again had a disappointing season, with Captain. Howard Marsh, finding it difficult, at times, to field a competent enough eleven, due to the side being made up of many of the promising Junior Players, without having enough experience in the side. Nevertheless, a respectable position was attained in the First Division of the West Midlands Third XI Club Cricket Championship. Next season will see Steve Russell in charge of the eleven, and the optimism is already high to improve on the 2009 season.

The First XI (Sunday)'s return to the First Division of the Warwickshire Sunday League, was short lived, and they finished bottom of the Division, prime candidates for the Second Division in 2010. There was always the difficulty of getting a strong enough side out, and skipper, Andy Stevenson, was always struggling to maintain a settled side. The best performance came from Steven Howard, in taking 6 for 26 against Dorridge, the second-best figures in the League, for the season. Others to put in useful efforts were, Paul Heron with his batting, Mark Guest, with both bat and ball, Sam Elgar, caught the eye, likewise, and Chris Hobbis always strengthened the batting when he was available, witness his top score of seventy-two runs.

It did not take Naeem Arif long to make his presence felt, after being made Captain, part of the way through the season, of the Second XI (Sunday). The first few weeks of the season saw the team in the bottom half of the Divisional Table, at the half-way stage the team were only one off the bottom of the table, but with one fixture to go it was between Sutton Coldfield and Olton & W.W. who were going to be Divisional Champions, unfortunately the title went to Olton & WW., but nevertheless it was an excellent effort from the team to be the runners-up. The two leading batsmen were Naeem Arif and Ben Wiseman, who made three and one half-centuries respectively, Jacob Brotherton also passed the fifty mark on one occasion, Lee Croucher was also likely to get runs. The best bowling performance came from Tom Eustace, who took 5 for 28, against Kenilworth, in the last match of the season. Other bowlers who featured with the ball, and took three and four wicket hauls were, Nasser Ali, Jack Holland, Kamram Fazal, Sem Rauf, Nahim Safdar and Ben Wiseman. With Naeem Arif moving up to Captain the First XI, Simon Broadhead will take over the reins of the Second XI.

Although not successful, the Third XI (Sunday), had a very enjoyable season, providing plenty of serious cricket for the many Junior Players that took part, this was, in no small way due to enthusiasm injected into the side by the Captain, Neil Horby, and Vice-Captain, Andy Sargent. With this type of approach this side will soon prove itself, even further, particularly as the Captain and Vice-Captain retain their positions.

The Junior Section were again well to the fore when it came to the sides competing in the Warwickshire and West Midlands Competitions, and it is a credit to the Managers and Coaches for all the time and efforts that they gave to their teams, particular mention must be given to Colin Greetham, who carries out the overall organising throughout the season, the team officials being Paul Heron, Graham Gomm, Andy Stevenson, John Howard, Steve Russell, Howard Marsh and Mark Guest. The Under l0s finished second in their North Birmingham League Division, whilst the Under 1 ls were in the top half of their table. The under 13s had a most rewarding season, they won their Division of the Warwickshire League, and they were winners of the West Midlands Cup, at their level. The Under 14s, had a average season, but still finished mid-table, so gaining good experience for the future. It was the double for the Under 15s, they won the West Midlands League and Cup at their level, and they are expecting to do well next season. Under 17s didn't fulfil their promise, due to the weather conditions, which affected several of their matches.

The outstanding player within the Junior ranks was Tom Banton, who made a great impression by scoring 203 runs in a match for Warwickshire Under 13s against Herefordshire, this performance earning him the Neil Abberley Award.

A very successful Annual Dinner and Presentation was held at the Moor Hall Golf Club, when the Club Awards were presented by the Guest Speaker, Dougie Brown, of Warwickshire County Cricket Club. The First XI (Saturday) Batting Award was made to Mark Guest, and Richard Norgrove received the Bowling Award. Martin Ball was given the Second XI (Saturday) Bowling Award. On Sunday, The First XI Batting Award went to Chris Hobbis and the Second XI Batting Award was received by Naeem Arif, whilst the Bowling Award went to Sam Sargent. The Carol Hansford Memorial Award was presented to Sam Sargent and the Terry Matthews Memorial Award, presented for the first time, was awarded to Tom Eustace. Junior Clubman of the Year for 2009 was Sam Elgar, and the Clubman of the Year was Paul Heron, in recognition of his work put in as Chairperson of the Ground Committee. Four stalwarts of the club were made Vice-Presidents, they were Jonathan Miller, in view of his Playing career, Mike Dean, for his organising the Annual Dinner, over a number of years, Hugo Russell, for his conscientious Umpiring of the Second XI, and to John Howard for his Committee work. Dignified Guests present were Alan Neal (Chairman of the M.C.C.C.), Robin Viner (Chairman of the B.& D.P.C.L.), John Reeves and Peter Barrel] (both Vice-Presidents of Aston Unity C.C.), John Day (Chairman of Water Orton C.C.) and Alan Wild (Harborne C.C.).

We would wish to thank some loyal Members who religiously put in a lot of work behind the scenes, those being Steve Smith, who is the scorer for the First XI on Saturday and Sunday, except when he is scoring for Australia, in a Test Match, Hugo Russell, who again gave his services as Umpire to the Second XI (Saturday), Annabelle Willets and Will Stone, for their assistance in providing the Match Teas throughout the season.

We were also fortunate to have the return of Colin Greetham as Groundsman, and Colin's services in that capacity have been greatly appreciated, Paul Heron, as Chairperson of the Ground Committee, as given good support in arranging Working Parties.
James Ross, President of Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club, is very pleased to receive the Honour of being made a Vice-President of the Birmingham & District Premier Cricket League.

Another honour to be bestowed upon a member of the club, is Peter Bell, who has, amongst other duties, the position of House Manager, Peter has been given the Award of Midlands Club Cricket Conference Cricketer of the Year - Administrative, which is the result of fifty years involvement in local Club Cricket.

We are grateful for the continued support from our Sponsors, namely, City Office Interiors, Simon John (Hair Design), Dave Bishop (Sportsco), Bracebridge (Estate Agents), Graham Gomm (Insurance), Robert Atherton (ACE Copying Limited) and Nigel Lyon (Pinstripe).

It is hoped that the year 2010 will see the club turn a corner in its fortunes, particularly from the playing point of view, there a lot of positive signs already appearing, so Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club are optimistic in their approach to the future.

entries.heading: Obituary to Philip G. Berry
paras: The Club’s membership was saddened to hear that Philip G. Berry, who was an umpire with the club between 1970 and 2004 passed away in a nursing home in Wendover near Amersham on the 16 February 2012.  Philip Berry (known affectionately as Phil) became involved with the Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club in 1970, when his son, Simon who as a 15-year-old school boy played for Bishop Vesey Grammar School against Sutton’s 2nd team. There was no scorer so Phil volunteered which was the beginning of a long association between Phil and the Club, and within a year Phil had put down the pencil and put on the white coat to umpire the second team who were without a regular umpire.

Within a season Phil was umpiring with the 1st team on Sundays and had taken umpiring seriously attending a training course run at Edgbaston and then joined Peter Bell in representing the MCCUA in the Jarvis Cup.  A national quiz competition on the Laws of Cricket, which the MCCUA team won in 1973.

Philip was born 15th December 1923 in Battle, Sussex and served in the Royal Navy during the 2nd World War as a Lieutenant posted to Aircraft Carriers.  Once released from military service Phil moved to Bristol and married Eileen in 1950 before moving to Sutton Coldfield in 1954.  One of Phil’s hobbies was the production of home-made beers for personal consumption and whenever you visited him in Jordan Road you were invited to visit his brewery under the stairs and sample the latest batch, but always warned don’t smell it before you sip it.
Phil also joined the Saturday morning beer line cleaning team and banking the cash weekly.  A job he carried out for some 20 years, although Phil did become a teetotaller.

In 1990 Phil was invited to join the Warwickshire Pilgrims annual tour of the West Sussex cricket clubs, being based at the Saffrons Cricket Ground in Eastbourne, which he did for some 10 years.  At the same time Phil was interested in raising the standard of umpires within the local cricket clubs joining the Sutton Coldfield branch of the Association of Cricket Umpires and became one of their instructors, progressing to become an ACU examiner of umpire candidates.

Phil as an umpire was very thoughtful, carefully taking a little time to decide, weighing up the fact in his mind before giving an impartial decision, whether it was for Pilgrims in Eastbourne, or for the Sutton Coldfield club or in a local game of cricket.  He was greatly respected for his knowledge and interpretation on the Laws of Cricket and was appointed to officiate in many Midland Club Cricket Conference games, and also in the Counties 2nd team games and in the 1979 International Cricket Conference Trophy matches.  The highlight of Phil’s career was being appointed to officiate in the Semi-final of the ICC Trophy between Bermuda and Canada and his cricket legacy can be seen in the 1980 Wisden Cricketers’ Almanack (page 316) – not bad for someone who never played any serious cricket, but devoted much of his time to the game of Cricket.

Phil had a very serious accident at home in 2004, which resulted him being hospitalized and in a coma for many months, before the family moved to Wendover, where Phil spent his last 6 years in nursing and care homes.
