GREETINGS from THE FAR EAST by JOE ILLINGWORTH

entries.heading: OWLS Captain 1986
paras: Many current SCCC members may not remember me, but I represented Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club from the early 1980s until the mid-1990s. I emigrated from England to Malaysia in 1997, the country of my mother, to witness a different type of life. I also enjoy the sun which is in plentiful supply in this far-flung equatorial paradise. One thing I didn’t expect to find was cricket!

The most popular sports played here are badminton, hockey, football, futsal and ‘Sepak Takraw’ (Kick Volleyball). The latter needs a lot of agility to keep a small ball made out of dried palm leaves airborne over a net. Only the feet, knee, chest and head can be used to touch the ball. I played it once and had back ache for weeks!

Not expecting to see cricket played over here, imagine my surprise then while driving to a supermarket, to pass a field where a game of the noble game was in progress. I immediately turned the car around so that I could take a closer look. I met the team coach, a Mr. Terry Tharma, an ex-state player, and whilst chatting with him, my love for the game was rekindled. A couple of weeks later I took to the field and bagged a couple of wickets. Bit lucky really, rank long hops which were top edged straight to midwicket. Lucky boy! And, oh yes, my batting is as boring as ever!

I have since found that there are a number of cricket clubs in Malaysia with various tournaments taking place. Many of the pitches are of the matting or artificial turf variety. However, a few of the bigger, more established clubs have natural grass strips. I had the opportunity to play at an international standard ground (Bayuemas Oval), not far from where I live, and which has been used as a venue for ICC matches in the past. I now represent the Royal Klang Club where we play mostly ‘village’ style cricket, though the youth team has been involved in a variety of tournaments.

Games are usually played in the afternoon. The T20 format is adopted mostly, though sometimes we play 25 or 30 over matches. One of the things I struggle with, are the lunches. You see, they serve lunch before we start and lunch isn’t something light. Instead, we are expected to tuck in to a feast of curry of various descriptions, fried chicken, fish, vegetables, rice and roti canai (a type of flatbread). You are stuffed before you start, unless you are careful! After the match it is the usual fare with plenty of beers, and yes, more curry!

When it rains, it really rains! However, it dries up quickly once the sun comes out. The humidity is around 80%, meaning that no sooner you have taken that long, cooling refreshing shower and got dressed, you feel like you need another one! I have got used to this over the years, but taking the field for 20 or 30 overs is challenging, though drinks are placed around the boundary edge to guard against dehydration.

It was fantastic to pop back to the club recently, while holidaying with my son. I see that my picture is still on the wall! Many thanks to Colin and Phil, who made me welcome with a warming drink of hot coffee, much needed! I also met Mike ‘run machine’ Hepburn who hasn’t changed a bit. As I gazed across the ground memories came flooding back and I admit I do miss playing on that lower ground.
Well, until the next time, ‘selamat tinggal’ (stay safe).

entries.heading: Andy Biddle
paras: Andy joined the Club as a schoolboy in 1981 and this year we all celebrated his 50th Birthday on 11th July, although the celebrations of this event commenced with Andy and Mike Mackey flying to the West Indies to watch England play in the 3rd test at the Kensington Oval, Bridgtown, Barbados which was won by the West Indies by 5 wickets.  Our troopers stayed at the same hotel as the England team and managed to fly home with them on the 6th May.  Andy found himself travelling alongside the England Captain, what a thrill for Andy to get first-hand how the game was won.  Never missing an opportunity Andy sought Alastair’s permission for a photograph.  Interviewing Andy back at the club, he referred to his meeting with Alastair as a very pleasant person to pass the time of day with, although Alastair made no mention of meeting our hero on his return to the UK.  Andy sponsored the B&DPCL game against Brewood C.C followed by a party open to all members. – a great way to celebrate your half century.

entries.heading: Highlights of 2015 Season
paras: Promotion again for the 1st team, as runners up to Bridgnorth C.C. and they will be playing in Division 1 of the B&DPCL in 2016 season, although it was a close-run competition with Bridgnorth just edging Sutton into the runners up position.

Although Sutton had the best of the encounters with Bridgnorth winning one game and a winning draw in the other d to rain curtaining the game. Sutton Won the B&DPCL T20 KO competition although having qualified for the final they were acknowledged underdogs, so it surprised everyone in the semi-final played at Bromsgrove C.C when batting first against Berkswell CC (a Premier League side) scoring 225 for loss of 4 wickets. Berkswell tried hard in reply, but finished 57 runs short.  In the second semi-final Barnards Green CC beat Shrewsbury CC by 8 wickets.  So, Sutton played Barnards Green (a division 1 side) in the final winning the toss and batting first but nearly threw it away when scoring only 132 all out in 16.5 overs. In reply Barnards Green batted steadily when scoring a run a ball. At the start of the 20th over Barnards Green needed seven runs to win. Lee Harrison bowled a tremendous last over, taking three wickets for only 3 runs. SCCC therefore won by four runs.

entries.heading: Highest Bowling Aggregate – Lewis Harrison with 9 wickets for 60 runs
paras: A great day’s cricket and reward for all our supporters who turned up on the day!
Match Report on Sutton Coldfield 1st team V The Legends team of 2003 on Sunday 5 July 2015

On the Waitrose/SCCC Open Day, the 2004 Legends won the toss and elected to bowl, which was perhaps a minor error in that the teary representing the current SCCC XI went on to score 280 for 8 off 40 over; with SCCC's usual No. 11 Dan Childs scoring 60 and being second man out when the score was already 150.  Further notable scorers were Marl Guest (skipper of the SCCC XI) who reached 57 off 41 balls; Steven Howard with 40 off 51 balls; and Lee Thomason who reached 45 off only 21 deliveries. Perhaps the most amusing incident occurred when Aaron, the younger of the two Thomason lads (now part of the future of Warwickshire County Cricket Club) got off the mark with a Chinese cut through his legs and then immediately got out to one of two catches, taken by SCCC 'Legend' Mike Dean — even more amusing was that Mike, himself a superb all-rounder for SCCC in 2004 and for many other years, couldn't actually manage to get a ball to the other end of a 22 yard strip in pre-game practice and then went on to get nought!  This was just one of the moments which provided a huge amount of amusement for the large number of onlookers. The Legends attack comprised Will Spear (0 for 48 off nine over); Andy Owen (1for 54 off six overs); Richard Norgrove (1 for 55 off nine overs) and Richard Seager (3 for 29 off seven overs), backed up by Sam Irvine who bowled four overs taking 1 for 23 and Jon Ship who took 2 for 52 off his five overs. All of the above showed they haven't actually lost it, but time has in some cases simply taken its toll! Sorry lads!

In reply to the challenging SCCC score, the Legends reached a very creditable 188 all out off 34.1 overs, with Jon Ship reaching a tremendous 83 off 66 balls, and Chris Munn and Mike Randall chipping in 6with 24 and 23 respectively.

All things considered it was a great game of cricket with the 'old men' showing more than a few glimpses of their talent, Hugo Russell gave up his Sunday to umpire at both ends and a large crowd thoroughly enjoyed themselves.  But, isn't that what cricket is all about?  Our thanks go to our local Waitrose Supermarket at Mere Green for sponsoring the game.

entries.heading: The 2004 Legends by Dan Davis (40th captain seasons 2005 – 2008)
paras: I've spoken with a couple of the guys from the championship winning side of 2004 and the most common thing that springs to our collective, ageing memories was just how much fun it was. They were very special times indeed and we also played some pretty good cricket along the way. Our opening partnership - Richard Dandy and Jon Ship - were two of the most talented batsmen I've had the fortune of playing with and you knew if their wickets were intact after 20 or so overs, you had a good chance of winning the game - whether setting a total or chasing.

Then there was the pro Tim Groenewald. Hard working doesn't even come close and its testament to his single-mindedness and work ethic that he's gone-so far in the game. Deano - you taught him everything, although he can't drink like a true Sutton great!

Speaking of Deano, or should I say 'The Legend of Sutton Coldfield Cricket Club', he was also a serious player. Bowling 27 overs down the hill whilst constantly hitting the seam would get most top league batsmen in trouble - and they frequently were.  I've still never seen anyone getting hit for a boundary take it more personally than the big man!!

Speero and Miller coming on first and second change and hooping it round corners also helped matters. They were both fairly high up in the banter stakes as well.  Ask Speer how he introduced himself to Deano whilst playing for local rivals Aston Unity.

There were also some younger players like Mark Guest, Sammy Irvine and Graham Clark coming in to the side and playing regularly too and I'm glad to see that they have gone on to realise the potential that they were showing in 2004 (not you Sam).

It is going to be a pleasure to come back and share memories with great friends who formed bonds on a sporting field (and in the bar) that will never be broken.  To anyone I've missed talking about from the 2004 side, I apologise. You can remind me how good you were later on.
Thanks very much for having us all back and here's to a great day back at the 'Rectory Utopia' (Paul Smith circa 2006).     Up the Royals!
